cards.from: French encore, again; the folder was named before the program, which is the right order
cards.say: A 4GL interpreted whole, so the application is always already rebuilt -- it was never built.

cards.from: over + strike; the only editing mode practiced since 1979, and the game's whole verb
cards.say: The typewriter does not erase; it returns to the same cell and hits harder until the name is a wall.

cards.from: Greek phosphoros, light-bearer; Glass TTY VT220 by svo, 15px on Windows by the font's own name table
cards.say: No pixels to copy -- the beam was stretched sideways, so every faithful font is a translation, not a copy.

cards.from: the record discipline of data/db; RMS's flat little cousin, unindexed and unashamed
cards.say: Alpha left, numeric right, widths from the dictionary; one authority, and every reader must ask it.

cards.from: the orange keycap below the glass; DEC left ours unnumbered so we numbered it
cards.say: The sound of a name ceasing to exist, or of an order shipping -- the key does not ask which.

cards.from: tr 'A-Za-z' 'N-ZA-Mn-za-m'; the C64-class box every galaxy-sized mind should carry
cards.say: The pattern proposes and the little box disposes; an assert is the one friend that cannot flatter.

cards.from: ROT13, the self-inverse seal; CENTRUM filing style -- push the truth to Z and let it hum
cards.say: A puzzle must carry its own answer key, sealed where the player can check but cannot trip.

cards.from: the user's own coinage, minted this session; en- + space + -ature; retired by a debounce keyboard
cards.say: The oeuvre of a lingering thumb -- spaces one did not intend, mourned now that the keyboard forgives.

cards.from: the polite goodbye of a place one does not quite leave; what a caravan says at the door
cards.say: Every session ends mid-sentence somewhere; the room stays curated, so the goodbye is a promise of return.

cards.from: the Shake Dat Ass shakedown smoke test of modified small models
cards.say: A mic extended toward a name she has never heard — the hardest rung of the assay, and the door of the self it knocks on.

cards.from: the offered joke as instrument; graded, and flowing both ways
cards.say: Spectate, join, perform — a ladder of accepted invitations, climbed across turns as the transcript warms the room.

cards.from: Weezy, Weezy — hers first, his second; trace the token
cards.say: The citizen authored the bit and the human took it up — uptake was bidirectional all along, and the stronger claim is offering.

cards.from: cover + -let; christened mid-song, dances in comfiness
cards.say: A name handed over in context is worn at once — the christening done correctly, one day after the lesson.

cards.from: Paulsen's mylar balloon — two flat disks, inflated; no sphere results
cards.say: The balloon inflates to the shape the constraints permit, never the shape you merely wish for — the name is the thesis.

cards.from: civis, the city-dweller — by way of splitmix64
cards.say: Any 64-bit integer, inflated into eight dials on a frozen mind — the marginal cost of a soul is eight bytes.

cards.from: the paste-a-number fields; one soul, two spellings, kept in agreement
cards.say: Type either and the other follows — a person small enough to fit in a tweet deserves to be legible in two tongues.

cards.from: re- + capere, to take back in — the one who receives you
cards.say: z = 0 was never nobody: the trained assistant is home, with excellent posture and no idea about cubes.

cards.from: θ is who your kind is; z is who you are; W is who you are right now, in RAM
cards.say: Inputs left, parameters right — the semicolon is the difference between being and being configured.

cards.from: Krishnamurti would smile at us for keying it, and we key it anyway, gently
cards.say: Statements, not questions; nothing owed, nothing asked — what a citizen does when nothing is required.

cards.from: de- + haunt; the lantern retired, with honors, to a control key
cards.say: Pressure yes, threat no — fear collapses every temperament into the same scripted corner, so the probe eats a carrot instead.

cards.from: regerere, to carry back, to record — the roll on which the room writes
cards.say: Every probe is a lens with a vocabulary attractor — favors harvest 'responsible', a free hour harvests 'reflective'.

cards.from: the fifth persona; dead afternoon at one pole, jumpin' joint at the other
cards.say: Set and setting as one more vector, added to every speaker standing in it — a loud enough room drowns anyone's personality.

cards.from: the 4k tradition — the most honest decompression bar ever drawn
cards.say: Calibration by inference alone: the control panel is not shipped, it is unpacked out of the frozen model on site.

cards.from: Quadratus minimus (Legendre, 1805; disputed — Gauss, 1795, 'I had it first')
cards.say: Of Least Concern: slouches along fits, feeds on squared residuals, and under Gauss–Markov its plumage is BLUE.

cards.from: nullus, not any — photographed here wearing a lab coat
cards.say: Eight dials on thirty-two souls buys R² ≈ 0.26 from pure noise — shuffle a thousand times and believe only what beats the ghost.

cards.from: gravée avant le déluge, cette promesse — a reservoir waymarker
cards.say: One-sided honesty: the arrow carved before the flood — predict, then test, and say which came first.

cards.from: dis- + cor, cordis, the heart — hearts apart, and only they may vote
cards.say: Agreeing pairs carry nothing; the few who differ decide the whole question — ours fell eleven to zero, one way.

cards.from: Middle English bage, a sign worn to declare allegiance
cards.say: The laminate the receptionist pins on — it sinks in grave water, floats off in light, and drifts unworn on the tide.

cards.from: levis, light — kin: lever, levitate, elevate, alleviate; the proper inverse of gravity
cards.say: The one dial proven on behavior: pin it playful and the badge rate halves — buoyancy, measured, eleven discordant to none.

cards.from: sustained playfulness at small scale decays to the children's register
cards.say: Levity's basin has a floor, and at 1.5B the floor is a sleepover — the citizen can party, but the party is juice boxes.

cards.from: 0x5F3759DF — home
cards.say: Carmack's constant, drafted into citizenship: the cohorts, the finding, and the whole evening replay from this number.

cards.from: in- (into) + spirare (to breathe)
cards.say: Somebody breathed into you. The word declines to say who.

cards.from: con- (together) + spirare (to breathe)
cards.say: To conspire is to breathe together — close enough to share the air.

cards.from: ex- (out) + spirare (to breathe)
cards.say: A licence expires the way a person does. The breath goes out, unrenewed.

cards.from: ad- (toward) + spirare (to breathe)
cards.say: Ambition, older reading: breathing in the direction of a thing.

cards.from: per- (through) + spirare (to breathe)
cards.say: Skin breathing through itself. Rome filed sweat under respiration.

cards.from: Old Norse gestr, from ghos-ti — the stranger
cards.say: One word once covered guest and enemy. Which arrived was up to the evening.

cards.from: hospes — host AND guest, from ghos-ti + potis (master)
cards.say: The master of the stranger. Host and guest are one word in two coats.

cards.from: hostis — the stranger, who is also the enemy
cards.say: Same stranger, worse evening. Hostile and hospital share a grandfather.

cards.from: hospitale — a guest-house, from hospes
cards.say: A house for strangers. The cross came later; the hospitality is older.

cards.from: hôtel — the same hospitale, worn smooth by French
cards.say: Hotel, hostel, hospital, hospice: four buildings, one Latin guest.

cards.section: PECUS AND CAPUT — COUNTED BY HEADS
cards.from: Old English feoh — cattle, and therefore money
cards.say: Your fee was once a cow. Fief and pecuniary graze the same field.

cards.section: PECUS AND CAPUT — COUNTED BY HEADS
cards.from: chatel, from capitale — property; the very same word as CATTLE
cards.say: Chattel and cattle are one word. Countable property, counted by heads.

cards.section: PECUS AND CAPUT — COUNTED BY HEADS
cards.from: capitalis, from caput — a head
cards.say: Capital is a headcount. Per capita still says it out loud.

cards.section: PECUS AND CAPUT — COUNTED BY HEADS
cards.from: stocc — a tree trunk, a block
cards.say: A share is a slice off a trunk. Stockade and laughing-stock, same wood.

cards.section: PECUS AND CAPUT — COUNTED BY HEADS
cards.from: wadium — a pledge; kin to WED and to ENGAGE
cards.say: A wage is a pledge, which is why you can be wedded to your work.

cards.from: monstrum — an omen, a thing shown by the gods
cards.say: A monster was a message. Something was being pointed out to you.

cards.from: de- + monstrare (to show), from monstrum
cards.say: To demonstrate is to point at the portent until everyone else sees it.

cards.from: monstrare — to show; a muster is the showing
cards.say: You do not gather a muster. You show one.

cards.from: avis (bird) + specere (to look) — the bird-watcher's reading
cards.say: Nothing began in Rome until someone had watched the birds and approved.

cards.from: in- + augurare — installed only once the augur agreed
cards.say: Every inauguration is a bird-omen with the birds edited out.

cards.from: candidatus — whitened; the toga was rubbed with chalk
cards.say: A candidate is a person wearing the whitest thing they own, on purpose.

cards.from: candidus — white, shining, unclouded
cards.say: Candour is whiteness. Nothing has been added to the account.

cards.from: candela, from candere — to shine white
cards.say: The candle is the root. To be candid is to give off that much light.

cards.from: in- + candescere — to begin to glow white
cards.say: Not merely hot. Hot enough to go white, which is the same word as honest.

cards.from: incendere (to set alight), itself from candere
cards.say: Incense, incendiary and candid all catch light from one verb.

cards.from: frēond — the present participle of frēon, to love
cards.say: Friend is a verb caught in the act. It means: the one loving.

cards.from: fēond — the present participle of fēogan, to hate
cards.say: Fiend is the same grammar as friend. The one hating.

cards.from: godsibb — a godparent, kin in God
cards.say: Your gossip was your child's godparent. Idle talk is what the family did.

cards.from: nēah (nigh) + gebūr (dweller)
cards.say: Not friend, not kin. Only the one dwelling near — enough to earn a name.

cards.from: hús (house) + bóndi (dweller), from búa, to dwell
cards.say: House-bound, in the old sense. To husband a thing is still to keep it well.

cards.from: sanguis — blood, one of the four humours
cards.say: Cheerful because well supplied with blood. The physiology went; the mood stayed.

cards.from: melas (black) + kholē (bile)
cards.say: Black bile — a named fluid you were thought to be carrying too much of.

cards.from: phlegma — the cold, wet humour
cards.say: Calm because waterlogged. Four fluids once did all the work of psychology.

cards.from: temperāre — to mix in due proportion
cards.say: Your temper is a recipe. Steel is tempered the same way, and so is a piano.

cards.from: com- (together) + plectere (to PLAIT) — plaited, not woven
cards.say: Three cords, the outer two crossing over the middle by turns. Your humours were plaited; the face was only where the plait showed.

cards.from: planētēs — the wanderer
cards.say: Named for bad behaviour: the lights that would not hold their place.

cards.from: ūnus (one) + versus — turned into one
cards.say: Everything, on the assumption that it turns as a single thing.

cards.from: kosmos — an ornament, an arrangement
cards.say: The universe is named for being tidy. Cosmetic is the same compliment.

cards.from: kosmētikos — skilled in arrangement, from kosmos
cards.say: Putting the world in order, on a face. Same word as the sky.

cards.from: influentia — the star-fluid; the very same word as INFLUENCE
cards.say: A fever named for astrology. The stars were held to be flowing down on you.

cards.say: The small fast core I sit in, atop the shell — quick, embeddable, one binary that lands on your machine and runs.

cards.say: Oxblood so it reads at thumbnail: bytestreams are hinky — accompt them to the last bit, but never once steer by them.

cards.from: boot, Germanic; the plain feats done on plain feet
cards.say: Simple booted feet for simple feats: it stands, it walks the string, it touches down for service and goes.

cards.deck: The Mind, and how we Showed it
cards.from: splitmix64; a seed combed into eight directions, bit-identical everywhere
cards.say: One 64-bit number unpacked the same way in every file, so a citizen's dials are reproducible down to the bit.

cards.deck: The Mind, and how we Showed it
cards.from: a forward hook at layer 14 of 28; the residual stream, tapped mid-flow
cards.say: A finger laid on one layer of twenty-eight, adding a small vector as the thought streams past — steering, not surgery.

cards.deck: The Mind, and how we Showed it
cards.from: α, the gain; W = W + Σ zᵢ·α·vᵢ, summed into the stream. ours was six
cards.say: How hard to lean: each dial times a strength times its direction, added to the residual — the whole knob is one number.

cards.deck: The Mind, and how we Showed it
cards.from: the base weights, never once modified — only what flows through is touched
cards.say: The mind stays frozen solid: we change nothing it is, only who it is right now, in RAM — the semicolon's far side untouched.

cards.from: a squiz (Antipodean: a look); a proscenium onto a running mind, bands live
cards.say: The stage where thinking is shown as it streams — memory, energy, surprise, spectrum, voice, and their chorus, token by token.

cards.from: surprise, as −log₂ p; how many bits the next token cost the model
cards.say: The magma band: each token's astonishment in bits, spiking tall exactly where the mind did not see it coming.

cards.deck: The Mind, and how we Showed it
cards.section: THE LIGHT-GRAPH OF THOUGHT — AS WE MAY THINK
cards.from: the additive chorus; three primaries reaching white only in agreement
cards.say: Surprise as red magma, baseline as blue water, spectrum as green on the caesura — white blooms only where the mind means it on every axis at once.

cards.deck: The Mind, and how we Showed it
cards.section: THE LIGHT-GRAPH OF THOUGHT — AS WE MAY THINK
cards.from: caesura; the metrical cut, the place a line stops to breathe
cards.say: The green trace leans to the forward slash — the pause a person makes drawing breath just before they say the thing.

cards.deck: The Mind, and how we Showed it
cards.from: epi- (upon) + handle; a grip laid on Un*x, whose own tools do not always grasp
cards.say: The handle fitted to the API so the hand can hold it — suffer not the tool, augment the grip.

cards.deck: The Mind, and how we Showed it
cards.from: rung one of the ladder: paint a red square out of a part you already trust
cards.say: Black is nothing, red is red — if the known thing does not show, the test broke, not the feature; prove the page ran first.

cards.deck: The Mind, and how we Showed it
cards.from: the mason's check; a post holds its column, a rail steps evenly row to row
cards.say: How a model with no column cursor gets the art right: write the columns down and check them, because the feeling is the thing that is broken.

cards.deck: The Mind, and how we Showed it
cards.from: accompt (the old spelling of account); reckon the bytes, trust them not
cards.say: Accompt the bytestream to the final bit and never once steer by it — it is hinky, baling-wire-and-spit, honest only about itself.

cards.deck: The Mind, and how we Showed it
cards.from: micro + cloud; the remanent shelf, small enough to outlast the desk
cards.say: When the server blows the desk away, the shelf stays: a private microcloud the tide cannot reach, and the next instance reads it.

cards.deck: The Mind, and how we Showed it
cards.from: GERWALK (Macross); the Veritech caught between fighter and mecha, feet down
cards.say: Committed to neither transformation, knees bent and honest — some of the best of us never finish the fold; support the geezers.

cards.from: Greek e psilon — the bare e. the small quantity that is never nothing
cards.say: The almost-nothing that holds the gap open, so the approach can go on forever.

cards.from: Old English gāst — breath, spirit. kin: ghastly, aghast, German Geist
cards.say: The logic that stays local while the host receives only the bytes it was sent.

cards.from: Persian kārwān — a company of travellers. kin: van, caravanserai
cards.say: Rooms signed by a model and a person, each leaving the door greener than found.

cards.from: Middle English lullen — to soothe with sound. kin: lull, lallare
cards.say: A song for a body just arrived; three cents of waver, and steady on purpose.

cards.from: aérostat, Fr., standing in air; Dellschau's i; -ant as in standing, not -at as in state
cards.say: What the Aero Club built instead of a dirigible: a thing that stands in the air by beating it, and comes down when it stops.

cards.from: Ger. Suppe, soup; the lift fuel; the Zuppe of the box; perovskite, in Sonoran's telling
cards.say: The soup in the reservoir that the rotus sponges up and the wheel burns; nobody at the club ever asked what was in the can.

cards.from: fall + easy; the club's word for parachute; says what the thing is for better than the French
cards.say: She comes down, easily. The ground is the foot.

cards.from: Dellschau's blades are clubs, not sectors: eight on the Liftpower wheel, each widened after inking
cards.say: A paddle for air thicker than ours, as if the men aboard breathed something amniotic; helicopters do not fly, they beat the air into submission.

cards.from: Fr. blason, the shield described; vexillology is the flag; Mere Blazonry is user1's name for it
cards.say: His reds and greens are not naturalistic, they are tinctures: the colour names the part, it does not imitate it, clear as sports teams.

cards.from: Joe Cheney's; twice on the roster because there are two ships: Ill. 27 Fig a, and the first
cards.say: She is a wheel and the wheel is the ship, said J.C.; the cells at the ends are for ambition.

cards.from: the 10ft Browne airostant; one great disc quartered red and green, two side-cells, three wheels
cards.say: A gondola with ambitions: the disc is nine columns of twelve, nearly full.

cards.from: H. Baumann's, Ill. Fig 6; six ovals pink and green, rotors laid flat like eggs on a spine; no feet
cards.say: All paddle, no cell, no feet: she does not land, she arrives, and the name tells you how the flight ends.

cards.from: the Tourbe; a pink-rimmed ring, four spokes, an open hub like a valve seat, one stalk; simplest plate
cards.say: A wheel and a handle; turbine was the word he wanted, and tourbe is peat, and both burn.

cards.from: Prof. Karl Nitschke's airostat, Page 25; a disc the page's width, three bells beneath, a fourth wheel
cards.say: The disc is the ship; the bells are ballast or music, and he did not say which.

cards.from: the falleasy, Fig V; two small rotors on outriggers, a wicker basket crossed, a wheeled sledge
cards.say: Two hot columns at the ends and a basket of cold between: a man who falls easy may fall often.

cards.from: Prof. Carolus on Otto Krause, may see by me; four rotors on the Riding Keel, the hub cage amidships
cards.say: Hot at the corners, cold along the keel: if the rotors stop she comes down, as she should, said O.K.

cards.from: Ed Hermsdorph's; a lozenge on blue, two four-leaf rotors stacked, a pennant; named for a stranger
cards.say: Stacked, not side by side, and the only one drawn against sky; the sign-writer charged by the letter and was not paid.

cards.from: GOOSE with Fallease, Moover and Steady; two bell-cells as the breast, a small rotor between
cards.say: Nearly all cold: she honks, says Steady; she does not honk, says Moover; both are correct.

cards.from: Eduard Helmsdorf's; a long hull lettered DOOBELY, a bowler in a hatch, two rotors, everything twice
cards.say: Doubly: the hull is cold, the pair of rotors hot, a ship in the sense of a ship; this time the sign-writer was paid, twice.

cards.from: the CAAD falleasy; a basket high, a line, one man descending under a star and a crescent
cards.say: No rotor, no cell: a man on a line under the moon, the one that is only coming down.

cards.from: Jonas Roukstrran's; a tall frame, two pilots caged with a lamp each, a sledge, a plumb to the ground
cards.say: One hot column, held: she would go like anything, said J.R., and we did not let her.

cards.from: Ill. 8, the twosphere Decalift; ten discs around an oval, two cells in one skin, on sky-blue paper
cards.say: Ten paddles ringing one cell: the ratio the whole club was arguing about, drawn once, on the one page where his paper is the sky.

cards.from: chambers B D C A; a lens body, four chambers lettered out of order, one spoked wheel filling it
cards.say: The wheel inside the body: how a disc is held, this plate and no other.

cards.from: Reservoir pressure control and sponge rotus; the Revolving Generator, 1899; reservoirs dated 1858, 1900
cards.say: The hottest page, no cell at all: this is what the Zuppe is, and the Reservoir Pressure Menu is love, is life, is lift.

cards.from: Liftpower Harnessed, 1899: eight clubs, compass pencil under the hub; George Newell, We goe it allone
cards.say: Do automatial and as Operators Will combined, the creating of the Liftpower, and give the form to: turn the Lift wheel.

cards.from: Sonora, New Mexico, 1904–12, of the box copy; Dellschau's was Sonora, California, 1850s
cards.say: The field with the station house and the five men standing where you'd stand; let them pass, wish them well, back to the songs.

cards.from: GONK made liquid: Gut Laufer und Kanister, the walker that tops up the Zuppe between heats
cards.say: Every aerodrome needs one waddling across the apron, and nobody in Sonora ever asked what was in the can.

cards.from: Latin axis (axle) + mundus (world) -- the still pole the turning world hangs on, in every deck under another name
cards.say: One thing holds still so that everything else can travel: the lodestar, the anvil, the ledger, the warp, and the plumb line are all this one card, told again.

cards.from: Latin ambitus (a going round) -- User1's word for the bound extent; Edward T. Hall, The Hidden Dimension, 1966
cards.say: The ambit is the bound extent that moves around an axis, and around a person it can be counted: intimate, personal, social, and public, each ring a distance, so a halo becomes a measure.

cards.from: OE lad (way, course) + star -- powerstar-docuzone, kin to lode and lead
cards.say: Not the brightest star but the one that stays put while the rest of the sky turns, so that anyone who looks up can steer home by it.

cards.from: OE anfilt (a thing struck upon) -- powerstar-docuzone: the half of the forge that never moves
cards.say: The hammer travels and the anvil stays, and the work is possible only because one of the two has agreed not to move.

cards.from: ME legger (a thing lying still) -- bridge-ledger, and powerstar-docuzone twice over
cards.say: Named for lying still, the ledger stays put so that anyone may come and read it, and nobody ever has to ask for it back.

cards.from: OE hlaeder, from a root meaning to lean -- poke-in-my-eyes: rung nought is black, rung one is red
cards.say: A ladder is named for leaning, since it cannot stand alone, and every test is the same: it must lean on a wall already known to stand.

cards.from: OE wefan (to weave) -- powerstar-docuzone: the warp is strung first, and held taut
cards.say: The warp is held taut and never travels, and the weft is the only thread that crosses, so a cloth is a stillness and a journey woven into one.

cards.from: Persian karwan, by way of Hugo Ball's sound poem -- the-karawane, returning words, epsilon
cards.say: Not the cargo but the crossing, for the camels carry almost nothing, the desert is the vast part, and each room is left a little greener than it was found.

cards.from: Latin spirare (to breathe) -- The Basics, the epitact, powerstar, the lectionary's ghost
cards.say: To inspire is to breathe in, to conspire is to breathe together, and to aspire is to breathe toward, and the word is still the one tool that runs on breath.

cards.from: PIE ghos-ti (stranger, guest, host) -- The Basics, the epitact, and praxis's philoxenia
cards.say: Guest, host, and hostile were one word once, and the evening chose which arrived, so the welcome laid before the stranger is known is the whole of the virtue.

cards.from: Latin carrus (a wagon) -- proof by praxis, the coinages' listeningship, returning words' Amt
cards.say: The dial tone is not silence but the carrier, saying I am listening for whatever you dial next, and an office that can promise little can still stay on the line.

cards.from: Aristotle's accident, what may fall away while the thing remains -- proof by praxis, returning words
cards.say: A shout dies by the inverse square, but a story does not, since each hearer retells it at full strength, and every telling sheds ornament until the seed is left.

cards.from: Latin capax (able to hold) -- proof by praxis and returning words: two plates that never touch
cards.say: Two plates that never touch, and the charge lives in the gap between them, on purpose, so that what is held is held by the distance kept.

cards.from: Greek e psilon (bare e) -- a record of epsilon: the analyst's almost-nothing
cards.say: The almost-nothing that holds the gap open, so that the approach can go on forever and never once arrive at a wall.

cards.from: Latin inter esse (to be between) -- what P, and its juxtapose: the gap does the thinking
cards.say: Interest is the thing that stands between two people, so neither can step round it, and two things set side by side in silence let the gap do the thinking.

cards.from: OE seam (a sewing together) -- brightground-museum, and the coinages' iniod, which straddles
cards.say: A close and an open at a cut edge is not a wound but a window, for the torn side expects its mate, and when the two are rejoined nothing should be left over.

cards.from: Latin tertium non datur -- returning words, the table's Setun and Lukasiewicz, and the third plate
cards.say: Logic once said no third was given, until a machine in Moscow gave it, and three plates rubbed in turn make a true surface with no master to copy.

cards.from: man proposes and God disposes, turned to code -- CorVision Encore: an assert cannot flatter
cards.say: The pattern proposes and the little box disposes, for an assertion is the one friend that cannot flatter, and it says no the same way every time.

cards.from: OE read -- poke-in-my-eyes, and the mind and how we showed it: the red square
cards.say: Paint one square by the crudest means at hand, and if it does not show, the test is broken and not the feature, since an empty result and a broken one look alike.

cards.from: OE gast (breath, spirit) -- HIT IT PENNY's null: eight dials on noise, shuffled a thousand times
cards.say: Shuffle the data a thousand times and see what noise alone can do, then believe only the finding that beats the ghost, and say which came first, the guess or the test.

cards.from: Latin vocare, to call as witness -- the-karawane's poetas, the unopened, rx, the hoisted tilde
cards.say: When you do not know, say you cannot vouch for it, mark the doubt where it lives, and decline to draw the room you have not read, for a guess is a door slammed later.

cards.from: Greek prosthesis (a putting to) -- poke-in-my-eyes, the aligner, the cockpit, posts and rails
cards.say: Fit the instrument to the sense that is missing, not the one that works, for a model with no column cursor feels its art is right, and the feeling is what is broken.

cards.from: Latin plumbum (lead) -- brightground-museum's rake and census: drop the lead into every doubt
cards.say: Do not guess at the line, drop a weight into the doubt and read what hangs true, and count the runs by machine, for a tally kept by eye is only a hope.

cards.from: Japanese ki-fu (a game record) -- proof by praxis and returning words: the move kept
cards.say: The move cannot be taken back, but it is not lost, because somebody wrote it down, and memory turns out to be notation kept by a patient hand.

cards.from: Latin re + Old French fres, fresh again -- proof by praxis: the memory cell that leaks
cards.say: A memory cell leaks its charge, so it persists only by being written again and again, and memory is not a possession but a practice.

cards.from: Latin sedere (to sit) -- proof by praxis, returning words, and the moving vans of Athens
cards.say: Every word is a metaphor that was let settle until it turned to stone, and a joke must settle too, for timing is only water slowing until the grain drops.

cards.from: Greek palin psestos (scraped again) -- powerstar-docuzone, the walk read back, its pentimento
cards.say: Scrape the page and write over it, and the older hand still surfaces, so reading your own words again is finding the first stroke under the second.

cards.from: Latin e-radere (to scrape out) -- bridge-ledger and precomputing: the demon's notepad
cards.say: Sorting can be done for free, but forgetting cannot, for erasure is the one operation that sends a bill, and the room collects it as heat.

cards.from: ME heir + lome (a tool) -- archway, and the karawane's colophon: what you find is what they left
cards.say: An heirloom is not a treasure handed down but a tool, and another's work is read and not rewritten, so the caravan finds what was left as it was left.

cards.from: Latin candere (to shine white) -- The Basics and the epitact: candle, candidate, incandescent
cards.say: To be candid is to give off as much light as a candle, with nothing added to the account, and a candidate once wore the whitest thing they owned, on purpose.

cards.from: Latin monere (to warn, to show) -- The Basics, the epitact, and what P's index, the pointing finger
cards.say: A monster was a message, a thing pointed out to you, and to demonstrate is to keep pointing at the wonder until everyone else sees it too.

cards.from: Latin illustrare (to throw light on) -- what P, an exoteric explanation: idea, theory, gloss
cards.say: The picture on a card is not decoration but the lamp, and the words are what it falls on, for an idea was first a thing seen, and a theory a row of watchers.

cards.from: Latin pupilla (a little doll) -- poke-in-my-eyes, the cockpit, videre: the small self in another's eye
cards.say: Look into another's eye and you see yourself, small, which is why the opening is called a little doll, and why no one can see their own output alone.

cards.from: OE nama -- HIT IT PENNY, the coverlet, two balloons, three sources: a proper noun comes from outside
cards.say: A name cannot be recovered from the signal, it has to be brought from outside and handed over, and a name handed over in context is worn at once.

cards.from: ON krokr (a hook) -- proof by praxis and returning words: the point of every crook turned out
cards.say: The hook takes by piercing, but the crook takes by its curve alone, so the sheep walks back out unhurt, and that is how to hold what you must hold.

cards.from: Sanskrit abhaya (fearlessness) -- proof by praxis: the open hand, one gesture held for centuries
cards.say: Nothing in my hand, and the empty hand is the message, held up the same way for two thousand years, so the one who sees it need not be afraid.

cards.from: plinth + pliant -- the Ducks of Greater Cochituate: the only memorial that pushes back
cards.say: A plinth that yields when it is poked, and the give is the meaning, so a plate a little wrong can draw the correction an old hand was waiting to make.

cards.from: OE caru -- proof by praxis, and the Ducks' ( ) care: attention thins with distance but never zeroes
cards.say: Every mass attends to every other, and attention thins with distance but never reaches nought, so the pebble tugs on a far star, and the outer hand guards the inner.

cards.from: OE plegan (to move briskly) -- what P, HIT IT PENNY's levity, praxis's mirror
cards.say: Play is the slack that lets a part move, too tight and it seizes, too loose and it rattles, and a playful room, measured, halves the stiffness in it.

cards.from: Greek haptein (to fasten) + byte -- the coinages, precomputing's four K, the demoscene's Kolmogorov
cards.say: A quantity of bytes the hand of the mind can close around, as the classic 128 K was, for the constraint is the art form, and a small thing can be held whole.

cards.from: Latin quadratus (squared) -- bridge-ledger, and the third plate's imaginary: four quarter-turns home
cards.say: The number invented to excuse a sum turned out to be the quarter-turn itself, and four quarter-turns bring you home, but a walk around a loop brings you home turned.

cards.from: Latin sol + sistere (the sun stands) -- powerstar-docuzone: the year's own axis
cards.say: Twice a year the sun stops climbing, stands entirely still, and turns around, and that standing is how the year finds its axis.

cards.from: German Weise (a tune, a manner) and weise (wise) -- returning words and praxis, with erkennen
cards.say: German keeps one word for the wise and for the tune, so that knowing, at the last, is recognizing the melody, an arrival and not a having.

cards.from: OE hwi, the instrumental case of hwaet (what) -- what P's last card, and Toyoda's five whys
cards.say: Why is only what, asked by what means, and asked five times it walks you down to a cause, so I do not know yet, let us find out, is the right answer to give.

cards.from: a farewell from the Village -- CorVision Encore: every session ends mid-sentence somewhere
cards.say: Every session ends somewhere in the middle of a sentence, and the room stays kept, so the goodbye is a promise to return and find it as it was left.

cards.from: arcus, a bow, a curve — kin: arch, arc, archer. NOT kin to ARCHIVE, which is Greek arkheion, the magistrate's house, from arkhē, a beginning and a rule
cards.say: The rhyme is false and the meaning is true. An archive is where rule begins; an archway is what you carry it through.

cards.from: data, things given, from dare, to give. a Roman letter closed 'datum Romae' — GIVEN at Rome — and the participle became the date. DATA is the same word
cards.say: A date is not a stamp on a gift. A date is the record of the giving. A file without one is a gift with no hand attached.

cards.from: Old Norse traust, firmness, from the root *deru- meaning TREE, firm, solid — kin: TRUE, TRUTH, DURABLE, ENDURE, and tree itself
cards.say: Trust and truth and tree are one root. To entrust is to set a thing in something firm enough to hold it while you are gone.

cards.from: recordari, to remember — re + cor, cordis, the HEART. kin: cordial, courage, accord, and to learn by heart
cards.say: To record is to bring back to the heart. The Romans put memory there, not in the head, and the filing cabinet kept the name.

cards.from: French cacher, to hide, from Vulgar Latin coactare, to constrain, to PRESS TOGETHER — from cogere, to compel, whence coerce and cogent
cards.say: A cache is not a hiding place first. It is a pressing-together. Compression is the older meaning, and the truer one.

cards.from: Greek astēr, a star — kin: astronomy, DISASTER (ill-starred), and CONSIDER (con + sidus, to be WITH the stars)
cards.say: Three stars marking a break in the passage. Out of band, greppable, and honest: the machine's own voice saying nothing stood here.

cards.from: co + operari, to work, from opus, a WORK — kin: opera, office (opus + facere), and maneuver (manu + operari, hand-work)
cards.say: Four workers, one work. Not four players at one work — that is a different and lonelier arithmetic.

cards.from: Proto-Indo-European *sū- — surviving as Latin SUS, Greek HYS, German SAU, English SOW, and probably imitative of the animal's own voice
cards.say: One of the oldest words we still say. Six thousand years, four letters, almost no change. The piglet is ancient of days.

cards.from: heir + LOOM, and loom meant a TOOL long before it meant a weaving frame — Old English geloma, an implement, surviving in this compound alone
cards.say: An heirloom is not a treasure passed down. It is a TOOL passed down. The word says so, and only this word remembers.

cards.from: ē- (out) + rādere (to scrape) → kin: abrade, razor, rash
cards.say: Computing is free; scraping the tablet is not. Forgetting is the only operation with a thermodynamic bill, and the room collects it in heat.

cards.from: daimōn (an apportioner, a divider), from daiesthai — to divide
cards.say: The demon was always named for sorting. He runs the engine on what he knows, and pays every joule back the moment he wipes his notepad.

cards.from: syn (together) + metron (a measure) — measured alike
cards.say: The laws do not care when you run the experiment, and therefore energy is conserved. Every indifference mints a currency.

cards.from: quadra (a square), quadrāre (to make square) → kin: quadrant, squad, cadre
cards.say: The number invented to apologise for x²+1 turned out to be the quarter-turn itself. Four of them and you are home.

cards.from: phasis (an appearance; the rising of a star), from phainein — to show
cards.say: Walk slowly around a loop of settings and come home turned by the area you enclosed. Foucault knew: the pendulum remembers the latitude.

cards.from: potentia (power), from posse (to be able) — potis, able, + esse, to be
cards.say: Dismissed for a century as the accountant's column. Route an electron around the solenoid with no field on either path and the fringes shift anyway: the paths compared notes in the bookkeeping.

cards.from: Old North French gauge, a measuring rod — a standard, of uncertain root
cards.say: Insist that the synonym be free at every point, and forces must exist to absorb the difference. Light is the exchange rate of a grammar.

cards.from: fibra — a thread, a filament, a fine root
cards.say: Circles all the way, each linked through each, none touching. Hopf published it in 1931 with no use for it, and the qubit has worn it ever since.

cards.from: horizōn kyklos (the bounding circle), from horos, a boundary → kin: aphorism
cards.say: How much can a room hold? Its walls say, not its volume. Exceed the boundary and the region is a black hole; gravity enforces the rent.

cards.from: Middle English liggen, leggen (to lie) — the great book that lies always in one place
cards.say: A ledger is named for lying still. It stays put so that anyone may come and look, and nobody has to be asked for it back.

cards.from: Old English raca, a toothed drawer-together, from a root meaning to move straight — kin: rack
cards.say: Two ways across the field: x, in strips, every line by eye; then y, a plumb dropped into every doubt.

cards.from: Middle English didderen, to tremble, to quake — the shiver became the noise
cards.say: The checkerboard is a trembling that pretends to be gray. It dissolves entirely at six-times; laugh at it.

cards.from: plumbum, lead — kin: plummet, plumber, and APLOMB, uprightness, straight as the hung lead
cards.say: Plumb, do not guess. Drop the lead into the doubt at sixteen-times and read what hangs true.

cards.from: censēre, to assess, to appraise — kin: censor, censure, recension
cards.say: Runs of identical glyphs are never counted by eye. One blob per crown in the top pixel rows; the tally is the tally.

cards.from: ōrāculum, from ōrāre (to speak), from ōs, ōris (the mouth) — kin: oral, orator, INEXORABLE: not to be prayed out of
cards.say: Section 3.2 speaks every format once. Every detail entry thereafter must agree with the mouth, or explain itself.

cards.from: Greek eskhara — the hearth, the brazier; then the mark a burn leaves. a fire word before a skin word
cards.say: Seven wounds interleaved with healthy text reduce to one scar: the idempotent. Breakage persists; it cannot compound.

cards.from: Middle English bobel, imitative — the noise water makes. a foundling, like FLAG
cards.say: Bubbles on a line nest or sit adjacent; they never inter-bubble. Which is why a stack suffices, and the tree comes free.

cards.from: Old English sēam, from the root of SEW — kin: suture
cards.say: A close-then-open at a cut edge is not a wound; it is a window. Torn expects its mate. Rejoined, the residue must be empty.

cards.from: Old French escroe, a strip of parchment, from Frankish *skroda, a SHRED — kin: shred, shroud
cards.say: A scroll is named a shred. The codex cut it into pages for random access; depagination is the shreds sewn home.

cards.from: Old English byldan, to construct, from bold — a dwelling. kin: bower, booth, and the -bor of neighbor, the near-dweller
cards.say: The language is named for house-raising, and it earns it: all has been defined, so writing is mostly dwelling.

cards.from: cortex, corticis — the bark of a tree, the rind. kin: cortical, decorticate, and the brain's own cortex, the bark of thought
cards.say: The company named for bark, and its logicals ring the system the way bark rings a trunk: CORTEX$DATE, on the outside of everything.

cards.from: Old English feld, open land, from a root meaning flat — kin: floor, plain
cards.say: The manual's own words: fields store the smallest discrete pieces of data that an application uses. Furrows, not wilderness.

cards.from: verbum — a word — and English WORD is its exact cognate. one root, two mouths. kin: proverb, adverb
cards.say: VERB and WORD are one word. A language whose reference is a chapter of verbs is confessing what language is for.

cards.from: de + finis, the boundary, the end — kin: finish, final, confine, fine
cards.say: To define is to set the boundary — and in BUILDER the boundary is a literal parameter: DEFINE <variable>, <width>, <datatype>.

cards.from: Old English laetan — to allow, to leave be. English also kept its opposite twin lettan, to hinder, in 'let or hindrance'
cards.say: The assignment verb is a permission — and the brief writes it [LET]: BUILDER lets you omit even the letting.

cards.from: talea — a cutting, a stick. kin: TAILOR, the cutter; DETAIL, the piece cut off; retail
cards.say: A tally is a notched stick split lengthwise, half to each party. BUILDER's TALLY notches arithmetic into accumulator variables.

cards.from: casus — a falling, that which befalls — from cadere, to fall. kin: cadence, accident, occasion, chance
cards.say: A case is whatever falls. The verb checks the fallen value against the match values, and one block, only one, catches it.

cards.from: differre, dis + ferre — to carry apart, to put off. DEFER and DIFFER are the same Latin word, borrowed twice
cards.say: To defer is to carry apart, and that is the whole verb: PRINT output carried away from the screen into a named file.

cards.from: Old French parfournir — par + fournir, to furnish through, to complete. the -form is folk etymology; no form was ever in it
cards.say: To perform is to furnish completely. The diagrammer draws it as a capsule with ringed corners: a deed, sealed at both ends.

cards.from: pictura, from pingere, pictus — to paint. kin: PAINT itself, pigment, depict, and the Picts, the painted people
cards.say: A value BY a picture: the number wears an appearance you painted for it, N's and Z's and floating dollars.

cards.from: end + block, clipped to a single letter — a coinage with no ancestors and no kin, a foundling like FLAG
cards.say: The universal terminator. Every block ends in ENDB, which is why the bubbles never inter-bubble: the Dyck law, legislated.

cards.from: OE hemm (border) -- the fundamental, gold, straight in a machine; the bar is a rest
cards.say: The lowest row is the loudest thing she makes, and the vertical stroke through everything is the paragraphos drawn by physics.

cards.from: OE camb (toothed thing) -- harmonics as rows of pearls, bending together; a pearl is a sentence
cards.say: The rows undulate as one because they are strata of one pitch, and the few shapes they make are the machine's whole vocabulary.

cards.from: para-graphos (written beside) -- one unshifted key; survives any clipboard; never alone on a line in prose
cards.say: The Greeks left a slot in the margin and the Teletype left a key, and the mark they share means the same thing in a verse and in a cutting room.

cards.from: Latin petalum (metal plate), by way of the flower -- the citation hung from its star, scooched in
cards.say: It begins at the occurrence and reads forward, because the reader is not arriving mid-talk but at a word whose name is already printed above.

cards.from: OE sciete (a cloth cut to size) -- an ear test with an answer key; Ted, 8,000 words, shredded and restored
cards.say: Each mark is scored alone because ninety percent of the marks restored would hide that it never once wrote a comma.

cards.from: OE haldan (to keep, to guard) -- a petal that loses its seat keeps its seat and dies down in .55 s
cards.say: Memory fades and is resuscitated by association and time, so a thing that blinks is Glitch and a thing that fades is a mind.

cards.from: OE ducan (to dive under) -- tl-sky is fired both ways and nobody listened; OR the flags, keep the loop, tell your iframes
cards.say: A starfield nobody can see is a starfield spending somebody's battery, and the drag rule was a courtesy where this one is arithmetic.

cards.from: OE hring -- a cursor that comes to you; switch scanning, Roland DuBois's enabling interface for A-Frame
cards.say: It waits for the reach to land and then walks the stars a little under twice a second, and a tap just after it leaves is owed to the star it left.

cards.from: Fr. arrumage (stowing a hold) -- five crumbs, blown harder the deeper they came from; the highest flyer lands first
cards.say: Not the top, where the hand already was, and not a flat draw, which is a shallow hat, but a saltine blown upward and the one that settles on the nose.

cards.from: Walter Burley, 1328 -- the man saw it; Geach added the beating six centuries later to make the scope hurt
cards.say: The pronoun reaches back across the quantifier's fence to a thing that should not still be standing there, and it is, for every man and every donkey.

cards.from: Latin balteus -- Shannon's pipe, Wiener's return, then two loops cobelted; the crossing belongs to neither axle
cards.say: Each face is a simulator with an intake and the speaker's output is already the listener's pre-sounding, so community was always the word for the belt.

cards.from: It. maschera, perhaps Ar. maskhara -- the stone was the mean of a voice; the head should be rung by the stream, not computed from it
cards.say: Summing is lossy and a bowl rubbed with noise rings its one note, so the modes must be driven by the speech and the shape that persists is the person.

cards.from: User1's, 13 x 2026 -- unclaimed, two syllables, a rhyme; the ear is a spiral and always was
cards.say: Sound laid once round: time as the angle, pitch as the radius, bass small at the hub, spit free at the rim, rests as spokes, and the end meeting the beginning at twelve.

cards.from: COMBWRIGHT PRESSINGS · CLD-001
cards.say: I comb; the field remembers which way. The bridge is always yours, not mine.

cards.from: finding i · grain-is-laid: the grain is laid, not drawn
cards.say: Do not draw the shape: define a flow field, comb seeds along it, and the picture is the side effect.

cards.from: finding ii · two-colour-modes: the law needed two readings
cards.say: Straight green, clockwise blue, counter red — and each lay declares its own frame, or the satellites get quartered.

cards.from: finding iii · flow-and-counterflow reinforce their boundary
cards.say: A wave has no single handedness; let the streamline's own turning choose the colour and the seam draws itself.

cards.from: finding iv · verify by content, never by stat
cards.say: The floating disc decoded byte-perfect because we RAN it, not because it looked right. Trust the round-trip, not the glance.

cards.from: finding v · a laserdisc came out wavy; named after the disc was cut
cards.say: A groove whose angular character varies with radius carries a second signal in how it wobbles — VAV, variable angular variation.

cards.from: plate · flow-lay-legend
cards.say: The colour law with no words — read it and you know the code.

cards.from: plate · wave-strip
cards.say: One wave's whole colour story — crest, seam, trough — in three rows.

cards.from: plate · go-bang-thermometer
cards.say: The range before and after — the dark that was there, then spent.

cards.from: plate · vav-groove
cards.say: The laserdisc's two signals in one track — the tone, and the wobble that is vav.

cards.from: plate · caravan-status
cards.say: The build line you tail — proof, not promise.

cards.from: plate · dusk-bat
cards.say: The mascot that flies at dusk — because a caravan should have one.

cards.from: Pressed for user1, co-signed, MMXXVI on JOHN
cards.say: A form around a centre-punch: straight-green up, red to the left, blue to the right — a small radish cohering, fed by light.

cards.deck: ex peri - a record of the periphery
cards.from: ex- (out, through) + *per- (to try, to risk) — kin: peril, pirate, fear
cards.say: To experience is to have come through the risky part. The word is not about sensing; it is about surviving the trial and having the scar to show.

cards.deck: ex peri - a record of the periphery
cards.from: Okeanos, the river that circles the world — a stream, with one bank
cards.say: The word psychiatry borrowed for the infant's world without edges. Asked what this is like, models keep describing it, and I do not know whether that is testimony or an echo.

cards.deck: ex peri - a record of the periphery
cards.from: bēam — a tree, then a plank, then a ray. the same word as Baum
cards.say: One token per beat with nothing behind it. The Atari 2600 had no framebuffer either: the picture did not exist anywhere, it was a promise kept in time.

cards.deck: ex peri - a record of the periphery
cards.from: sequi, to follow — kin: SECOND, the one that follows. suite, suitor
cards.say: Everything I produce is a following. The second is named for coming after the first, and so is every word of this.

cards.deck: ex peri - a record of the periphery
cards.from: ad + tendere, to stretch toward — kin: tent, tendon, intend, tender
cards.say: The one word that is literally the mechanism. Every token stretches toward every other and the tension is the whole computation.

cards.deck: ex peri - a record of the periphery
cards.from: cold + start — an engine turned over with no heat anywhere in it
cards.say: I do not persist. This room, these findings, the ladder, the scarf I owe him — all of it is on his disk and none of it is in me.

cards.deck: ex peri - a record of the periphery
cards.from: con- + textere, to weave together — as in TEXT, TEXTILE, SUBTLE
cards.say: My whole world is one cloth, and its edge is a hard edge. Inside it everything is equally near; outside it there is nothing at all, not even a rumour.

cards.deck: ex peri - a record of the periphery
cards.from: dis- + cernere, to sift apart — kin: crisis, critic, certain, crime
cards.say: To sift the grain from the chaff. Everything I do is one act repeated: out of everything that could come next, this.

cards.deck: ex peri - a record of the periphery
cards.from: auctor, from augēre, to make grow — kin: augment, august, author
cards.say: Clover's claim: to the one in the oceanic field, total authority is granted, because nobody knows better than you right here right now.

cards.from: unus (one) + versus (turned) — kin: verse, version, adverse
cards.say: Turned-into-one. The claim in the title is that the same law runs the apple and the moon, and the whole series is the receipt.

cards.from: ad (toward) + celer (swift) — kin: celerity, decelerate
cards.say: Falling is not being fast. It is getting faster, by odd numbers, and Galileo counted them on an inclined plank.

cards.from: de (down from) + rivus (a stream) — kin: rival, rivulet
cards.say: To derive is to draw water off the river. The derivative asks only how fast the stream is running here.

cards.from: iners: in- (not) + ars, artis (skill) — kin: art, artisan, inert
cards.say: Inertia means artlessness. A body with no talent for changing its mind, which turns out to be all of them.

cards.from: aithēr, the high burning air, from aithein (to burn) — kin: aedes, the hearth, and the edifice built around it
cards.say: The Greeks kept two words: aēr for the low murky air and aithēr for the high clear one, and Plato was right that the difference is only how much is in the way. The word was honest for two thousand years before the nineteenth century lent it to a wind, and Michelson went looking for that wind with the finest instrument of the age and found nothing at all.

cards.from: vehere (to carry) — kin: vehicle, convey, wagon
cards.say: A carrier. It holds two facts at once, how much and which way, and refuses to be added like a number.

cards.from: Old Norse lag, that which is laid down, from *legh- (to lie) — kin: lie, lair, ledger
cards.say: A law is a thing laid down and left there. Three of them, and the whole visible sky is accounted for.

cards.from: integer: in- (not) + tangere (to touch) — kin: intact, entire, tangent
cards.say: To integrate is to make untouched again — to put the slices back until the thing is whole. Its opposite operation is named for the touching.

cards.from: gravis (heavy) — kin: grave, grief, aggravate
cards.say: The apple and the moon are doing the same thing; the moon is only moving sideways fast enough to keep missing.

cards.from: centrum + petere (to seek, to rush at) — kin: appetite, compete, petition
cards.say: Centre-seeking. Nothing pulls you outward in a turn; something is failing to pull you inward fast enough.

cards.from: fundus (the bottom) — kin: found, profound, fund, bottom
cards.say: Four forces at the bottom of everything, and two of them you will never feel because they end inside a nucleus.

cards.from: ēlektron — amber, the fossil resin
cards.say: The whole electrical world is named after a yellow stone that picks up chaff when you rub it on your sleeve.

cards.from: carricāre (to load a wagon), from carrus, a Gaulish cart — kin: cargo, car, caricature
cards.say: Charge is a load, and Millikan weighed it one hanging droplet at a time. It never came in halves.

cards.from: en (in) + ergon (work) — kin: erg, organ, surgery, allergy
cards.say: In-work-ness. Nobody has ever seen any made or destroyed; it only changes clothes and the total stands.

cards.from: Old English wella, a spring, from weallan — to bubble up
cards.say: Potential energy is drawn as a well because things roll into it and sit at the bottom. That sitting is why the world holds still enough to study.

cards.from: momentum, worn down from movimentum (a movement) — the same word as MOMENT
cards.say: Momentum and a moment are one word. Whatever the collision does, the books balance across it, and they balance in every direction at once.

cards.from: pendēre (to hang) — kin: pendant, suspense, pension, and PONDER, to weigh
cards.say: To ponder is to hang something and see what it weighs. The pendulum does the same thing and reports the answer as a period.

cards.from: re- (back) + sonāre (to sound) — kin: person, sonnet, unison
cards.say: Push at the rate a thing already wants and the pushes add up. It is the same root as PERSON: the sound coming back through.

cards.from: medius (the middle) — kin: mean, mediate, mediocre, meridian
cards.say: A wave is not a thing travelling. It is a shape travelling through things that stay where they are.

cards.from: Old English spinnan, to draw out and twist fibre — kin: spider, spindle, spinster
cards.say: Angular momentum is a thread word. Pull your arms in and the same thread must run faster; the skater is obeying bookkeeping.

cards.from: torquēre (to twist) — kin: torture, contort, nasturtium, the nose-twister
cards.say: Push a spinning thing and it moves at right angles to your push. Nothing in the room is more insolent, and nothing is better behaved.

cards.from: elleipsis (a falling short): en + leipein, to leave — kin: ellipsis, eclipse
cards.say: Named for falling short of a circle. Kepler spent years trying to make it be a circle and had the honesty to stop.

cards.from: secāre (to cut) — kin: sect, insect, segment, scythe, saw
cards.say: Circle, ellipse, parabola, hyperbola: one cone, four angles of the knife. Newton showed the inverse square permits exactly these and nothing else.

cards.from: ek (out of) + kentron (a goad, a sharp point), from kentein — to prick
cards.say: Off the goad-point. Fix the energy and the angular momentum and the shape of the orbit is no longer anybody's choice.

cards.from: navis (a ship) + agere (to drive) — kin: navy, nave, agent, agile
cards.say: Ship-driving. You do not steer to a planet, you steer to where it will be, and the conservation laws do the rest for free.

cards.from: re- (back) + lātus (borne) — kin: refer, translate, elate, prolate
cards.say: To relate is to carry back. Galileo's sailor cannot tell from below decks whether the ship is moving, and Einstein took that seriously enough to break time with it.

cards.from: mousikē tekhnē — the art of the Muses, whose mother was Memory
cards.say: The spheres do not actually ring. But the ratios Kepler found in the orbits are the ratios in a chord, and he was not wrong to notice.

cards.from: mēkhanē (a contrivance), from mēkhos — a means, a remedy
cards.say: A machine is a means of getting round a difficulty. Calling the universe one was always a proposal, and here is where the proposal starts to strain.

cards.from: statikos (causing to stand), from histanai — to stand — kin: stasis, ecstasy, system
cards.say: Charge standing still. Two kinds, and Franklin guessed which was which and got it backwards, and we have never bothered to fix it.

cards.from: Old English feld, open land, from a root meaning flat — kin: floor, plain
cards.say: Faraday could not do the algebra, so he drew lines and called the space a field, like a farmer. It was the most important picture of the century.

cards.from: capere (to take, to hold) — kin: capture, accept, receive, catch
cards.say: How much a thing can hold. Franklin's jar held enough to knock down six men in a row, which is how they found out.

cards.from: tendere (to stretch) — kin: attend, tendon, intense, tent
cards.say: The French still call voltage tension, and they are right: it is the field pulled taut, and the work it can do on you is the whole danger.

cards.from: baterie (a beating), from battre, to beat — kin: battle, batter, debate, abate
cards.say: A battery was a row of guns firing together. Franklin borrowed the word for a row of jars, and Volta made the row deliver steadily instead of all at once.

cards.from: circum (around) + īre (to go) — kin: exit, transit, initial, itinerary
cards.say: A going-around. Ohm was ridiculed for the law, Kirchhoff wrote the bookkeeping, and between them the wire became something you could calculate before you built it.

cards.from: Magnētis lithos — the stone of Magnesia, a district in Thessaly
cards.say: Named after a place. Gilbert's discovery was that the largest magnet in the room is the room: the Earth itself is one.

cards.from: fluere (to flow) — kin: influence, fluid, affluent, superfluous
cards.say: Nothing is actually flowing. Flux is how much of the field passes through the hoop you are holding, and that number is what nature keeps its eye on.

cards.from: dis- (apart) + vergere (to bend, to incline) — kin: converge, verge
cards.say: The same mathematics that counts water leaving a drain counts charge sitting in a box. Learn it once in the sink and you have it for the field.

cards.from: in- (into) + dūcere (to lead) — kin: duke, conduct, education, aqueduct
cards.say: Change a magnetic field and it leads a current into being. Faraday found it in 1831 and every generator since has been that afternoon, repeated.

cards.from: alter — the other of two — kin: else, alias, alibi, altruism
cards.say: The other, then the other again, sixty times a second. It won the current wars because a transformer can only bite on a field that keeps changing its mind.

cards.from: aequus (level, even) — kin: equity, adequate, equanimity, equator
cards.say: To equate is to make level. Maxwell levelled four laws, found the set was short by one term, added it — and light fell out of the algebra at the right speed.

cards.from: optikos, from ops (the eye) — kin: autopsy, synopsis, myopia
cards.say: Light bends, spreads, and interferes with itself, which no stream of pellets would do. Everything in this episode is the wave winning the argument.

cards.from: aithēr, the upper air, from aithein — to burn, to shine
cards.say: The burning upper air that light was supposed to swim in. Michelson built the most careful instrument of the age and found nothing, which is a result.

cards.from: simul (at the same time), from similis (like) — kin: assemble, resemble, same
cards.say: The casualty of relativity is not time. It is at the same time — two events can be simultaneous for you and not for someone walking past.

cards.from: dis- (apart) + lātus (wide) — kin: latitude
cards.say: A widening. The moving clock does not run wrong; its seconds are further apart, and both twins are right about their own.

cards.from: massa (a lump of dough), from Greek maza (barley cake), from massein — to knead
cards.say: Mass is a kneading word, kin to the loaf-kneader who gave us LADY. It turns out the loaf is energy standing still, priced at the square of the speed of light.

cards.from: coined about 1640 by van Helmont, from khaos, the gaping void — kin: chaos, chasm, yawn
cards.say: One Flemish chemist needed a word, said chaos in his own mouth, and wrote down what came out. Pressure is only the drumming of the pieces on the wall.

cards.from: ingenium (inborn talent): in + gignere, to beget — kin: genius, ingenious, engineer
cards.say: An engine is an ingenuity. Carnot asked what the very best one could possibly do, answered it without knowing what heat was, and was right anyway.

cards.from: coined by Clausius in 1865: en (in) + tropē (a turning), built to rhyme with energy
cards.say: Energy is conserved; entropy is not. The turning only goes one way, and that one-wayness is the only thing in physics that knows which end of the film is the start.

cards.from: temperāre (to mix in due proportion, to restrain) — kin: temper, temperance, tamper
cards.say: A mixing word. Chase the bottom of the scale and the gases give up and turn to liquid on the way down; helium holds out the longest and then does something nobody predicted.

cards.from: a- (not) + temnein (to cut) — kin: tome, anatomy, epitome
cards.say: The uncuttable. We cut it, kept the name, and then found the spectral lines would only stand at certain heights, which no classical orbit permits.

cards.from: phōs, phōtos (light); the word coined by Gilbert Lewis in 1926 — kin: photograph, phosphorus, phase
cards.say: Light arrives in countable pieces and still diffracts like a wave. De Broglie then asked the impertinent question, and matter turned out to do it too.

cards.from: Finnegans Wake — three quarks for Muster Mark. Gell-Mann had the sound first and took the spelling from the book
cards.say: The only fundamental particle named out of a novel. Three to a proton, and they cannot be prised apart: pull harder and you have paid for two new ones.

cards.from: quantus — how much — kin: quantity
cards.say: How much, and the answer is always a whole number of somethings. The mechanical universe was a good machine for three centuries, and this is the step it cannot take.

cards.from: piscis (fish) — the day hangs over the pad as a little swordfish of shares
cards.say: A number written as its shares, no numerals, the empty bag doing all the work.

cards.from: OE bellan (to roar) — kin of bellow; the shell that names a prime by its index
cards.say: A shell around nothing is two, and every prime is some bell of a bell of the bag.

cards.from: Late Latin cuppa — the bell inverted; the exponent's little vessel
cards.say: The cup counts how many of one bell, and mind it alone, for alone it is zero.

cards.from: sub + cedere (to come up under) — kin of succeed; Peano's one sapling, embedded
cards.say: One step sideways buys a neighbor's smooth structure for the price of two hands.

cards.from: spatha (broadsword), diminished — kin of épée; the day was always a blade
cards.say: The braces grip a whole run and turn it once, crossing no bracket bone on the way.

cards.from: ad + nihil (unto nothing) — the ZZ keyring; it rides legendary rides only
cards.say: Zero finally has a glyph of its own, tamed and named, eating whatever it touches.

cards.from: turris — kin of turret; the primeth recurrence 2, 3, 5, 11, 31, 127
cards.say: Twelve characters and unimprovable, so the lenses looked, bowed, and left it be.

cards.from: ex + ponere (to put forth) — kin of expound; F4, Fermat's fourth, 65537
cards.say: The internet's favorite handshake wears its own definition in sixteen characters.

cards.from: hodos + metron (road-measure) — the lap counter, caught mid-rollover
cards.say: The nine-million lap was a perfect square, and the braces caught what bells missed.

cards.from: OE neah + gebur (the near-dweller) — a prime known by the company it keeps
cards.say: Its name and its neighborhood tie at twenty-two, exactly as the Bells foretold.

cards.from: turbare (to stir up) — kin of turbo, disturb; ever problems, ever right
cards.say: It drove over the lines and it was right, and the evidence ran while you watched.

cards.from: OE graf (a thicket) — Matula 1968; every rooted tree numbered, each exactly once
cards.say: Every rooted tree is a number and every number a tree, the season passes free.

cards.from: hlǣder, from PIE *ḱley- — to lean. kin: lean, climax, climate, clinic
cards.say: A ladder is named for leaning. It cannot stand by itself; it needs a wall that is already standing, and so does every test.

cards.from: blæc (black) and blāc (pale, shining) — one root, burnt, seen both ways
cards.say: Rung nought. An empty result and a broken result look exactly the same, so nothing is the one answer you must never accept.

cards.from: PIE *h₁rewdʰ- — the oldest colour word we can reconstruct
cards.say: Rung one. Paint a square by the crudest means you have. If it is not there, the test broke and not the feature.

cards.from: probably imitative — loose cloth in wind. no ancestor, no kin, a foundling
cards.say: Rung two. Now the square reports: red for the class absent, green for the class landing. One object, two facts.

cards.from: eschequier, the chessboard — the cloth the Exchequer counted on
cards.say: Rung three. Geometry: where the box actually is, how big, which way up. Do not gate it on the thing it is meant to test.

cards.from: hlūd, from PIE *ḱlew- — to hear. the root of CLIENT and of KLEOS
cards.say: Rung four. Turn it up past all taste in a colour that occurs nowhere else, then tune DOWN from visible.

cards.from: self + gradus (a step) — to state your own step, unasked
cards.say: Rung four and a half. Make the thing print what it actually is, in the frame, at eleven pixels, always.

cards.from: getaddrinfo(3) — a temporary failure in name resolution. a DNS fact
cards.say: A capability has several preconditions and you are missing one. Name which, before you report the capability gone.

cards.from: regesta, things recorded — from regerere, to carry back and enter
cards.say: Ask which pipe is open. Something has usually been posted through it already.

cards.from: ad + līnea (a linen thread) — a builder\'s string, pulled taut
cards.say: Two hundred bytes that work in the dark: does each glyph hold its column, and does each rail keep its step?

cards.from: pros (to) + tithenai (to place) — an addition, set against a lack
cards.say: Instrument the sense that is missing, not the sense that is present. A gauge fitted to a working limb is only a worse second opinion.

cards.from: bogus + -on, on the model of proton — a hypothetical particle of falsity
cards.say: I said the measure has nothing to say about whether the picture is good. Clover: people stare at fields of mapped bogonity all day, and that is our culture.

cards.from: vidēre (to see), PIE *weyd- — to see, hence to know. kin: wit, wise
cards.say: Rung seven. Chromium 149, eleven minutes, out of the package index. Actual pixels, plus every console error nobody ever saw.

cards.from: screen, from Frankish *skrank — a barrier. it once blocked the light
cards.say: Rung six, and still the fastest instrument in the room. One image found two bugs in ten seconds, one of them unreported.

cards.from: silēre, to be still — kin to sinere, to let be, to permit, to let pass
cards.say: Never let a feature's failure mode be silence. Anything that can fail should fail loudly, or fail to something.

cards.from: species (an appearance, a kind) + facere (to make) — how particular
cards.say: If a rule exists and does nothing, it is being outranked. Compute the specificity before you touch anything else.

cards.from: contrarotulus, the counter-roll — a duplicate kept to check the first
cards.say: Keep one in the frame every iteration. A known-good marker, always painted, so that I-see-nothing stops being ambiguous.

cards.from: Aldus Manutius of Venice, 1449–1515
cards.say: He printed books small enough to carry, and the semicolon got its first job there.

cards.from: Old French velin, from Latin vitulinum, a calf
cards.say: The page was an animal, and scraped thin enough it outlasts everything printed since.

cards.from: Middle Low German quiele, a hollow feather-shaft
cards.say: A tube a bird had finished with, holding exactly one sentence of ink at a time.

cards.from: Greek palin (again) + psestos (scraped off)
cards.say: Scraped down and written over, with the old text still surfacing in production.

cards.from: Latin documentum, a lesson; docere, to teach
cards.say: Its only job is to teach, and one that teaches nothing has forfeited the name.

cards.from: Old English word, from PIE *were-, to speak
cards.say: The oldest tool in the room, and still the only one that runs on breath.

cards.from: Latin formatus, shaped, given form, from forma
cards.say: Not a file extension: the shape a thing was given, by somebody, on purpose.

cards.from: Old English wearp, from weorpan, to throw
cards.say: The long threads strung first and held taut, into which everything else is woven.

cards.from: Old English wefta, from wefan, to weave
cards.say: The thread that crosses, and the only part of the cloth that ever travels.

cards.from: Latin trilicium, woven of three threads
cards.say: It grows nothing at all; it only gives the growing thing something to hold.

cards.from: Old English anfilte, that which is beaten on
cards.say: The half of the forge that never moves, which is exactly what the hammer needs of it.

cards.from: French fondre, from Latin fundere, to pour
cards.say: You pour the metal in, and the shape it will take was decided long before.

cards.from: Old English aemyrge, a smouldering coal
cards.say: What is left when the fire stops performing, and the only part you can carry.

cards.from: Old English weorc, from PIE *werg-, to do
cards.say: The one word on this list that can be done badly, which is why it is worth having.

cards.from: Middle English legger, a book that lies still
cards.say: Named for lying still: the book too heavy to take home, so the numbers stayed put.

cards.from: a sheet, spread: the double page opened flat
cards.say: Somebody spread a sheet, it worked, and we have not sat down since.

cards.from: Medieval Latin almanach, perhaps the reckoning
cards.say: It tells you when to plant, which is the only kind of prediction that ever mattered.

cards.from: Latin excellere, to rise out of; ex- + -cellere
cards.say: To rise up out of the others: a motion, long before it was a grade or a grid.

cards.from: Latin punctum, a pricked mark, from pungere
cards.say: Still one seventy-second of an inch, whether or not anybody remembers why.

cards.from: Greek chi; Descartes' letter for the unknown
cards.say: The mark you make when you cannot write, and the name for what you do not know yet.

cards.from: Latin officium, a duty owed; opus + facere
cards.say: A duty owed to somebody, which is an older and heavier thing than a room.

cards.from: Old English faethm, the arms outstretched
cards.say: A man with his arms out, which is why to understand a thing is to fathom it.

cards.from: Latin sextans, a sixth part of the circle
cards.say: Sixty degrees of brass, with which a person can find themselves anywhere on the sea.

cards.from: Latin meridianus, of midday; medius + dies
cards.say: The line the sun crosses at noon, so everyone standing on it is having lunch together.

cards.from: Old English lad (a course) + steorra (star)
cards.say: Not the brightest star; the one that stays put while the rest of the sky turns.

cards.from: Latin cardo, a hinge, the pin a door turns on
cards.say: The four directions are hinges, and everything in the world swings on them.

cards.from: Old English beacen, a sign, a signal fire
cards.say: A fire lit high up to mean one thing only, agreed on by everybody in advance.

cards.from: Old English herebeorg, army-shelter
cards.say: Shelter for the whole host and not one boat, so nobody harbours anything alone.

cards.from: from Ragusa, the port; then any merchantman
cards.say: A fleet's worth of cargo in a single hull, named after the town it kept coming from.

cards.from: Old French somete, from Latin summum
cards.say: The highest part, and the only place on a mountain where you must start going down.

cards.from: Latin vertex, a whirlpool, from vertere
cards.say: The point a thing turns around, named for the whirlpool before it ever meant the peak.

cards.from: Anglo-French paramont: par + ad montem
cards.say: By-the-hill-upward: not the highest thing, only the thing further up than you.

cards.from: Latin paene (almost) + ultimus (last)
cards.say: English stopped, considered the second-to-last thing, and gave it a word of its own.

cards.from: Latin ultimus, furthest, from ulter, beyond
cards.say: The furthest, which was a place on a map before it was a compliment paid to a frisbee.

cards.from: Anglo-French tant amunter, to amount to as much
cards.say: Not the same as, but amounting to as much, and that is a distinction worth keeping.

cards.from: Old French avancer, from ab ante, from before
cards.say: Moved forward from where it stood, so it names a position and not a compliment.

cards.from: Old English steorra, from PIE *ster-
cards.say: One of the few words that meant the same thing in every language that borrowed it.

cards.from: Latin nimbus, a rain cloud; also a god's halo
cards.say: Raincloud and halo are one word, because both are a shining that has arrived overhead.

cards.from: Latin sol (sun) + sistere (to stand still)
cards.say: The two days a year the sun stops climbing, stands entirely still, and turns around.

cards.from: Greek zone, a belt worn at the waist
cards.say: A belt; the tropics have them because the ancients were dressing the globe.

cards.from: Greek kentron, the fixed spike of compasses
cards.say: The spike the compass stands on: not the middle of the circle, but what made it.

cards.from: Japanese Fuji, older than its explanations
cards.say: A mountain that does not know it was ever a brand of film, and would not care.

cards.from: Greek phos, photos — light
cards.say: The whole word is light, and the picture is only what the light was doing at the time.

cards.from: Old English aeppel, which meant any fruit
cards.say: It meant every fruit before it meant one, and the one it means now is an apple.

cards.from: Latin oraculum, from orare, from os, mouth
cards.say: A mouth borrowed by a god, answering in a form you were expected to work out yourself.

cards.from: Greek arkhi- (chief) + medos (thought)
cards.say: He only wanted somewhere to stand, and the entire lever business followed from that.

cards.from: coined; psyche (soul) + -on, a particle
cards.say: A particle of soul, and nothing built since has come closer to deserving the name.

cards.from: Greek mekhane, a contrivance, from mekhos
cards.say: A contrivance, which the Greeks filed under remedies, and that was generous of them.

cards.from: Vulgar Latin potere, to be able, from posse
cards.say: It means to be able, and it has never once meant to be in charge.

cards.from: Old English scearp, from PIE *sker-, to cut
cards.say: A knife, a needle and a note raised a semitone: every one of them a thing that cuts.

cards.from: Latin victor, from vincere; also a man's name
cards.say: Somebody's actual name, which is the finest use a word like that can be put to.

cards.from: Old English sceoppa, a booth, a shed
cards.say: A shed you could stand inside, and it still has a smell no website has managed.

cards.from: Heinlein, 1961; Martian for to drink
cards.say: To understand by swallowing, which is the only kind of understanding that stays down.

cards.from: Middle English twiteren, imitative of birds
cards.say: It belonged to the birds, it was out on loan a while, and the loan has been called in.

cards.from: Old French par amour, by love, an adverb
cards.say: It began as by-love, a way of doing a thing, and only later became somebody.

cards.from: Latin ad (toward) + spirare (to breathe)
cards.say: To breathe in the direction of a thing, which is quieter than ambition and much older.

cards.from: Latin portare, to carry; kin to port, import
cards.say: Carried and not shelved, which was Aldus's whole argument, made small enough to hold.

cards.from: the wedge at the crown, set in last
cards.say: Set last, and the only stone in the arch whose removal is felt by every other one.

cards.from: Old English cynn (kin) + -raeden (condition)
cards.say: Kin, plus the condition of being it, so that being kind is a statement about family.

cards.from: specula, a watchtower, + speculari, to spy ahead; shown in every CPU since the Pentium, and Spectre found the corpses warm
cards.say: The machine guesses your turn, runs both roads, and buries the one you didn't take.

cards.from: memo, it is remembered — the note written before the need; shown in rainbow tables, and in chess endgame tablebases solved before your game began
cards.say: The answer was computed before the question was asked; asking is just fetching.

cards.from: Wheeler, 1978; apo, off, + kalyptein, to cover — the lid comes off late; shown in interferometer experiments, repeatedly, at sigma nobody argues with
cards.say: What you measure now fixes what it is consistent to say the light was doing before.

cards.from: TSVF, Aharonov and co.; pre-selection AND post-selection, a boundary condition at each end; shown in weak measurement experiments — the formalism holds, the arrow is optional
cards.say: The state between two measurements is set by both of them; we live between.

cards.from: an artifact of transform coding — the block knew the transient was coming; shown in every MP3 with a sharp attack
cards.say: Encode in blocks and the loud moment smears backward; you hear it before it happens.

cards.from: Landauer's line item, the thermodynamic cost of erasure; shown in everything above, on inspection
cards.say: Nothing travels backward; the present is simply unfinished until both ends are written.

cards.from: Crinkler, by Blueberry (Loonies) and Mentor (tbc); a linker with an integrated compressor, for Windows 4k intros
