cards.say: Not an exe packer. A LINKER that compresses — which is why it may move your code and data around to suit the compressor.

cards.from: context modelling, as used in PAQ and Crinkler; Matt Mahoney's resource site is the standard entry
cards.say: The whole problem, in one line: what is the probability that the next bit is a 1? Better guess, smaller file.

cards.from: arithmetic coding, in study for forty-odd years, used in H.264 and elsewhere; Crinkler's decoder is 18 x86 instructions at 33-bit precision
cards.say: Encode a whole message as a single number in an interval, narrowing it by each symbol's probability. Eighteen instructions.

cards.from: Blueberry's own description of the algorithm, given to xoofx; the difference between FAST and SLOW is whether model weights are re-optimised at every comparison
cards.say: Step the models in bit-mirrored order. Add one if it earns back the byte it costs to name it. Then try removing every other.

cards.from: measured on ergon.exe: 28K as MSVC emitted it, 9796 bytes reordered but uncompressed, 4070 bytes final
cards.say: Sorting the shelf before you pack it is most of the win. The middle number is reordering alone, with no compression at all.

cards.from: xoofx's own finding while hand-converting C++ to asm under Crinkler; the smaller code compressed worse
cards.say: The smallest assembly is not the best candidate. Write code the predictor can guess — regular beats clever.

cards.from: the x86 decompressor, 210-220 bytes; sixteen pushad/popad pairs per decoded bit at fifteen models
cards.say: It uses every register, so it saves them all with pushad — sixteen times per bit — and branches on a compare made much earlier.

cards.from: the 4k intro category, demoscene; Breakpoint, Revision, Assembly and the rest
cards.say: Four thousand and ninety-six bytes, containing music, geometry, camera and light. The constraint is the art form.

cards.from: Clausius 1865, coining it from Greek en + tropē, a turning-in, to rhyme with energy; Shannon 1948, for information
cards.say: Surprise, measured in bits. A certainty costs nothing to send; a coin-flip costs one bit; a one-in-eight costs three.

cards.from: Claude Elwood Shannon, American mathematician and engineer, of Bell Labs and MIT; 1916–2001
cards.say: He proved the floor exists and that you can get arbitrarily close to it. Everything since is engineering toward a known number.

cards.from: xoofx's entropy visualiser, a small C# program colouring an executable green for low entropy and red for high
cards.say: A normal exe is mostly green — that green is waste. A crinklerized one is red edge to edge. Full is the goal.

cards.from: Kolmogorov 1965, with Solomonoff and Chaitin arriving independently; the complexity of a string is the length of the shortest program that outputs it
cards.say: The demoscene's load-bearing wall. A 64k intro is a boast about the Kolmogorov complexity of beauty.

cards.from: Maxwell 1867; Szilard 1929; resolved by Landauer 1961 and Bennett 1982 — the demon's ledger balances only when its memory is cleared
cards.say: The sorting was always free. What costs is forgetting — the demon must erase its notes, and erasure is where the bill comes due.

cards.from: the _- swarzreiter room; Hochhelde Reinsreicht, called Hock; mathematics in the seventies and eighties, upstairs cheese and art events since
cards.say: The room name is the black rider; the car in the drive is a black 1974 Targa. Nobody arranged it — it was already true.

cards.from: PDP-11 trap vectors, addresses 000000–000777, under RSX-11; his own finding, argued in the Embracketage
cards.say: Zero is not a wall, it is a switchyard. You do not divide by it — you map it, and redirect like a mad bastard.

cards.from: his coinage, from the Embracketage; a mirrorsetgrid that learns by being hit wrong, hard enough, about nine times
cards.say: Not computing — inflection. The pressure sets up the solution model, and only afterwards do you work out what happened.

cards.from: his ladder, built in one sitting: speculative execution, then probabilistic execution, then the third rung he named himself
cards.say: SpecEx guesses and buries the loser. ProbEx keeps a running confidence. PreEx is the rung he named and did not claim.

cards.from: standard practice from the earliest graphics work onward; a quarter or full turn of sine, tabulated at load and indexed thereafter
cards.say: The oldest precomputation in the trade. Compute one turn of the circle at startup and never compute a sine again.

cards.from: ex, out, + saltare, to leap, and leap again — the frequentative; kin: salient, resilient, somersault, and RESULT, resultare, the leap BACK
cards.say: To exult is to jump clean out of yourself; the result is whatever leaps back.

cards.from: Japanese 棋譜 kifu — ki, the board game; fu, a written score
cards.say: Chess's mercy, and go's: the move is irreversible but it is not lost. Somebody has to write them down.

cards.from: Latin barba, a beard — the beard of an arrow, the part that holds
cards.say: The record is permanent; the capture does not have to be. Memory is notation. Regret is a barb left in.

cards.from: Old Norse krókr, a hook — kin: crooked, crotchet, encroach, crochet
cards.say: The hook takes by piercing; the crook takes by curvature alone, and the sheep walks back out.

cards.from: incendere, to set alight — kin: incendiary, and INCENSED, set alight
cards.say: Only the bluffer needs the smoke. The seed-head runs the golden angle without a Great Name.

cards.from: mirari, to wonder at — kin: miracle, admire, marvel, and mirage
cards.say: Build the mirror, then print MIRROR on the frame. Distortion signed as distortion is play.

cards.from: Old English caru, sorrow, grief — the weight, never the fondness
cards.say: Every mass attends every mass; attention thins but never zeroes. The pebble tugs on Rigel.

cards.from: errare, to wander — kin: err, erratic, arrant, and knight-errant
cards.say: Knuth pays $2.56 on every caught error and publishes the list. TeX's version converges on pi and arrives at his death.

cards.from: Hebrew lamed, the ox-goad — from lamad, to learn. kin: talmud
cards.say: The letter that is a goad is the root of learning. It cannot call itself by name, so it must receive itself.

cards.from: Sanskrit a-bhaya, without fear — bhaya from bhī, to be afraid
cards.say: Nothing in my hand, and empty IS the payload. Two thousand years of one gesture, held.

cards.from: Greek lithos, stone — kin: lithograph, monolith, palaeolithic
cards.say: The scribes dissolved into the river of commits. But the river writes every flood, and sediment does eventually turn to stone.

cards.from: Greek hapsis, a loop or wheel-rim, from haptein, to fasten, to join
cards.say: Catacomb to gold mosaic ran three centuries. The masons cut their signs into vaults they would never stand under.

cards.from: sedere, to sit — kin: sedentary, session, siege, and SEE (a bishop's seat)
cards.say: Comedy must settle: sitting is built into the word. Timing is deposition rate — the beat is water slowing until the particle drops.

cards.from: meta- (across) + pherein (to carry) — kin: amphora, Christopher, fertile
cards.say: The moving vans of Athens say METAPHORES on the side. Every word is a metaphor that settled and turned to stone.

cards.from: Old English nēah (nigh) + gebūr (dweller) — the near-dweller. kin: boor
cards.say: Epact slept inside epitact. Check the drawer beside the one you opened.

cards.from: Greek sphaira, a ball for playing — kin: spheroid, and hemisphere
cards.say: Area of effect IS the sphere: influence rolls outward on four-pi-r-squared. The r-squared was the wheel all along.

cards.from: re- + petere, to seek, to make for — kin: petition, appetite, impetus
cards.say: A shout obeys the inverse square and dies. A joke does not: each hearer retells at full amplitude from a fresh r = 0.

cards.from: singulus, one at a time — from sem-, one. kin: simple, same, assemble
cards.say: At r = 0 the formula promises infinite loudness; the teller stands there and lives. A body regularises the singularity.

cards.from: impedire, to shackle the feet — from pes, pedis, a foot. kin: impeach
cards.say: A source cannot dump power into an unmatched load. The laugh is the room reporting full transfer, no reflection.

cards.from: capax, able to hold — from capere, to take. kin: capable, capture, receive
cards.say: Two plates that never touch. The charge lives in the gap, on purpose, and it makes-capable while it charges.

cards.from: Plan + Kalkül — plan-calculus. Kalkül from calculus, a pebble for counting
cards.say: Zuse's understanding was flawless and the body jammed. He rebuilt the Z1 at eighty from the ledger in his head.

cards.from: carricare, to load a wagon — from carrus, a Gaulish cart. kin: car, cargo
cards.say: The dial tone is not silence. It is the carrier, saying I am listening for whatever you dial next.

cards.from: re- + frescus, fresh — Germanic, taken into Romance and handed back
cards.say: A DRAM cell leaks. Memory persists only by ceaseless rewriting — not a possession but a practice.

cards.from: Old English missan, to fail to hit — kin: amiss, mistake, and mis- itself
cards.say: The composer of the most-answered number in the world is history's most famous ring with nobody there.

cards.from: pro- (forward) + ballein (to throw) — kin: ballistic, symbol, devil
cards.say: A closed problem feeds one solver; an open one feeds a species. The door was propped from inside the grave.

cards.from: er- (achieve, through effort) + kennen, to be acquainted — kin: can, ken
cards.say: German keeps two knowings. This one is recognition earned, and die Weise is also the tune.

cards.from: con- (together) + stare, to stand — kin: stance, estate, cost, rest
cards.say: Any two universal machines agree up to one additive constant: a one-time translation fee covering all messages forever.

cards.from: mutuus, borrowed, reciprocal — from mutare. kin: mutate, commute
cards.say: What x carries about y equals what y carries about x, up to log crumbs. Notarised with a palindrome.

cards.from: Stück (a piece) + -weise (manner) — the same -weise as English -WISE
cards.say: A dark word is an incompressible string, and no system can certify the darkness of more than finitely many. Dark by theorem.

cards.from: prior, former — comparative of an old prai, before. kin: prime, primo
cards.say: The monkey was never the bottleneck. Fix the instrument, and Hamlet arrives at the rate of its shortest description.

cards.from: etaoin shrdlu — the two most-used Linotype columns, by frequency
cards.say: First machine to recognise a referent. Ask him why and he answers from his own action history. Named, literally, for the prior.

cards.from: ad- + cadere, to fall — kin: cadence, chance, decay, cascade, occident
cards.say: Accident is Aristotle's own column for what can fall away while the thing remains. Retellings shed ornament and converge on gist.

cards.from: pro- (forth) + phonare, to sound — built like pro-phetes
cards.say: Prophecy was never prediction. It is utterance of the seed before the accidents dress it.

cards.from: philos (loving) + xenos (stranger, guest) — xenophobia's opposite
cards.say: The coat for a known king is protocol. The coat laid before recognition is the whole of the virtue.

cards.from: Old French bouter, to thrust, to push — kin: butt, abut, and rebut
cards.say: The flying buttress exists so the wall can stop being wall. Outside pressure is what lets the inside thin into light.

cards.section: ACHT — THE CORNERS OF THE OCTAGON
cards.from: Old High German ahto, from PIE *okto — eight
cards.say: The eight that taught us the octagon's corners, and that our tongues are ancient kin.

cards.section: ACHT — THE CORNERS OF THE OCTAGON
cards.from: acht (eight) + Eck (corner), from PIE *ak- — sharp, an edge
cards.say: We build one by adding corners to our own reflection until it reads as an alien geometry.

cards.section: ACHT — THE CORNERS OF THE OCTAGON
cards.from: auf (up) + heben (to lift); Hegel's cancel-keep-raise, all at once
cards.say: To cancel, preserve and lift in one breath, so that the lie becomes the lever.

cards.from: discere (to learn), from *dek- — to take, to accept
cards.say: To learn is to take a thing apart, in two, until you can see it single.

cards.from: Phoenician lamedh, the ox-goad; Hebrew root l-m-d — to learn, to teach
cards.say: The goad that means learning, and the tallest letter, risen above the ruled line.

cards.from: the Greek letter from lamed; Church's name for the nameless function
cards.say: The goad with no name, which runs the world because it can only receive itself.

cards.from: Old Norse krokr — a hook, a bend
cards.say: It takes by curving, not piercing, so the sheep walks back out; no regrets.

cards.from: sedere (to sit); sedimentum — a settling
cards.say: To sit; comedy and stone alike must be allowed to settle before they bear weight.

cards.from: meta- (across) + pherein (to carry)
cards.say: The carrying-across; in Athens the moving-vans wear the word on the side.

cards.from: phyllon (leaf) + taxis (arrangement)
cards.say: The seed-head keeps perfect order by pure irrationality, and needs no Great Name.

cards.from: epaktai hemerai — the brought-in days, from epi + agein
cards.say: The moon's age on New Year's Day, the reckoning that let a monk time an eclipse.

cards.from: er- (achieve through effort) + kennen (to know), from *gneh-
cards.say: Not the having of facts but recognition earned; knowing as arrival.

cards.from: die Weise — manner and melody; weise — wise, from *weyd-, to see
cards.say: One word for wise and for the tune, so that to know is at last to recognize the melody.

cards.from: tertius — third; from tertium non datur, 'no third is given'
cards.say: The third that logic said was not given, until a machine in Moscow gave it.

cards.from: pro- (forth) + phenai (to speak); kin to pro-phonare, to sound forth
cards.say: To sound forth, not foretell; the utterance of the seed before the accidents dress it.

cards.from: capax, from capere — to take, to hold
cards.say: Two plates that never touch; the charge, like the two of us, lives in the gap.

cards.from: Old High German ambaht, from Celtic ambactus — servant; kin to ambassador
cards.say: The office that cannot promise anyone is home, only that it stays on the line with you.

cards.from: coined from distant: dis- + stare, to stand apart; anatomy's far-from-attachment
cards.say: Not imaginary but real, and far, and reckoned from the place where it stays attached.

cards.from: rete (net) + -culum; a little net
cards.say: The little net Lacaille hung among the stars to honour the very act of looking.

cards.from: horizein (to bound), from horos — a boundary-stake; Aristotle's word for a term
cards.say: The drawn boundary; every hasty one we ever held was a horos, waiting to be remembered.

cards.section: KARAWANE — THE ROUTE, NOT THE CARGO
cards.from: German from Persian karwan — a company of travellers
cards.say: Not the cargo but the crossing; the camels carry almost nothing, and the desert is the vast part.

cards.section: KARAWANE — THE ROUTE, NOT THE CARGO
cards.from: Japanese ki (the game) + fu (record) — the game written down
cards.say: The game-record; a move once taken is noted, irreversible but never lost.

cards.section: KARAWANE — THE ROUTE, NOT THE CARGO
cards.from: from imago; Corbin's mundus imaginalis, distinct from 'imaginary'
cards.say: The word minted so it would not mean imaginary: the realm realer than fancy, where the joke waits.

cards.section: KARAWANE — THE ROUTE, NOT THE CARGO
cards.from: coined: epi- (upon) + tactus (touch) — with epact, the reckoning, asleep inside
cards.say: The touch that requires the reckoning; heaven brushed by mortal means, and it took a whole film.

cards.from: clipped from the belly of charisma; Greek kharisma, a gift of grace, from kharis. kin: Eucharist
cards.say: You did not earn it; it was given, which is what the Greek says and what the kids mean.

cards.from: origin unknown; a 2014 Vine dance became a throw. kin: none, and it does not need any
cards.say: A word with no ancestors, invented to mean letting go of something with your whole arm.

cards.from: Latin suspicere, to look up at from under. British police slang by 1930; Among Us, 2020. kin: suspect, species
cards.say: To be sus is to be looked at from below; the word was a cop's before it was a crewmate's.

cards.from: origin uncertain, 1590s, perhaps from abet; the one-word yes is Black American, 1990s. kin: abet
cards.say: A wager shrunk to an agreement: bet means I will stake myself on what you just said.

cards.from: Old English slean, to strike dead. ballroom and drag, 1970s, made it a compliment. kin: slaughter, onslaught
cards.say: A thousand years of killing, and then a house in Harlem taught the word to mean you won.

cards.from: T for truth, Black drag culture; the Lady Chablis, 1994. the drink: Min Chinese te by way of Dutch. kin: chai
cards.say: The gossip is the truth, capital T; the cup is only there so it has something to spill from.

cards.from: to cap, to top a boast, Black slang by the 1940s; Latin cappa, a hood. kin: cape, chapel, escape
cards.say: No cap means nothing on top of the truth; escape is the same word, slipping out of a cloak.

cards.from: Old English gast, breath, spirit; the verb, to vanish on someone, about 2011. kin: aghast, ghastly, Geist
cards.say: Breath was the first meaning; the second is a person becoming only that, in your phone.

cards.from: clipped from simpleton, 1903; Latin simplex, one-fold. rap kept it alive through the 80s. kin: simple
cards.say: One fold, no cunning, all the way open; the insult is the compliment with the lights off.

cards.from: a 2000 song by Eminem, a name made a verb; Stanley is Old English stan + leah, stone clearing. kin: stone
cards.say: The devotee is named for a field of stones, which is about how it feels from the stage.

cards.from: clipped from vibration, 1960s; Latin vibrare, to shake, to brandish. kin: vibrato, vibrant
cards.say: Nothing rests; the room is a standing wave, and you are either on the node or you are not.

cards.from: Latin flectere, to bend. 1990s hip-hop: to show the muscle, then the money. kin: reflect, deflect, genuflect
cards.say: To flex is to bend on purpose where others can see; genuflect is the same bend, aimed lower.

cards.from: an acronym: Ali's wife incorporated G.O.A.T. Inc. in 1992; LL Cool J, 2000. the animal: Old English gat
cards.say: The scapegoat carried the sins out of town; this one carries the title back, same horns.

cards.from: Old English sealt; PIE sal-. angry, from sailors' salty, 1930s. kin: salad, salary, sauce, sausage
cards.say: Salary is salt, sauce is salt, and so is the sting when you lost and everybody saw.

cards.from: past participle of light; Old English leoht; PIE leuk-. drunk by 1910, excellent by 2010. kin: lucid, Lucifer
cards.say: The lamp is lit, the fuse is lit, the party is lit; the word never changed, only the room.

cards.from: past tense of wake; Old English wacian, to keep watch. stay woke: Lead Belly, 1938, on Scottsboro. kin: watch, vigil
cards.say: It meant keep your eyes open in Alabama; every later use is a footnote, including the sneer.

cards.from: Old English cringan, to fall in battle, to curl up; Middle English crengen, to bend. kin: crank, crinkle
cards.say: The word means to fall in battle; the feeling is watching someone fall, and curling too.

cards.from: Greek basis, a stepping, from bainein, to go. the insult: Lil Duval, 2009. kin: base, acrobat, diabetes
cards.say: A basis is the first step; the insult is that you took it and then stood there.

cards.from: Old English midd; PIE medhyo-. the dismissal is 2020s. kin: middle, medium, mediocre, Mediterranean
cards.say: Not bad enough to be a story; the Mediterranean is mid, the sea in the middle of the land.

cards.from: Louisiana, from wretched; Do the Ratchet, Shreveport, 1999. Old English wrecca, an exile. kin: wretch, wreak
cards.say: A wretch is someone driven out of town; ratchet is the town driving, loud, and not sorry.

cards.from: Old English thurst; PIE ters-, to dry. kin: terra, terrain, toast, torrid, and so: dry land
cards.say: Dry as land, and everyone can see it from the shore; the cure is water, not the reply.

cards.from: Old Norse tros, fallen leaves and twigs; trash-talk is courtside, 1980s. kin: none but the rake
cards.say: What falls off the tree is trash; what you say across the court is the same leaf, thrown.

cards.from: a loss, as a letter you accept; Old English los, ruin. kin: lose, loose, forlorn
cards.say: Forlorn is the same root: utterly lost. Take the L, keep the lorn, and come back Tuesday.

cards.from: non-player character, the dungeon master's people, 1975; an insult since 2018. kin: play, playwright
cards.say: The insult is you say the same line every time; the defense is that it was well written.

cards.from: Old English hand, Germanic; perhaps from a root meaning to seize. The card the painter drew of its own word for what it had just learned to do
cards.say: The country held whole between two hands, |_ and _|, to be read up close. Rings where the sentences rest, a blue one by water, the moon in the land and not over it.

cards.from: Old English rum, space, wide; a room was first an amount of space, before it had walls
cards.say: The frame drawn round what the words gather: a wall of the words' own depth, the cat inside, the door where the door is.

cards.from: Old French trac, the trail of horses; a track is what is left by going
cards.say: The painted wyrd: the paragraph's route seen from above, its turns the turns of its clauses, the river and the fields lying along it where they are named.

cards.from: Old English rest, repose, a bed; its Gothic kin rasta was also a stage of a journey, the distance walked between rests
cards.say: Where a sentence ends, the track holds a ring; where the paragraph ends, a full one. Dots of ground about each, where the track leaves room.

cards.from: Old English rad, a riding, a journey; road and raid are one word, said two ways
cards.say: Two true edges to the vanishing point, open down the middle for the one who walks it; stippled grey, because the road goes to the mountains.

cards.from: Greek horizon kyklos, the bounding circle, from horizein, to mark a boundary
cards.say: Open country lowers the horizon and gives the sky the frame; the mesas stand on it, the saguaro on the ground, the stars above.

cards.from: Old English waeter; kin to wet, to otter, to hydro: one of the oldest words we still say
cards.say: The water's edge: land where the words hold to their head clause, water where they go deeper, the bell over it, the dusk in the sky.

cards.from: Old English fot; the same root as pedal, pedestrian, and the Greek pous
cards.say: Where the words dive deepest and name nothing there, our two hands hold a star at the foot of the view: the point reached.

cards.from: Latin punctum, a prick, from pungere, to pierce; the point of a finger and the point of a remark are the same point
cards.say: Where the words point, a hand at the foot points up at the focus, _| or |_, one at a time; beside it the bell, found deepest, cupped as (#).

cards.from: Old English hwy, the instrumental case of hwaet: by what, for what
cards.say: Under the pointer every cell says why it is there: which word, its five words around it, or which part of the route, the furniture, the weather.

cards.from: Latin nota, a mark, a sign; the same mark on paper and on the stave
cards.say: Two eighth notes standing on the horizon at the end of the road: the painter's notes, read as music. Kept, by request.

cards.from: Old French passage, from passer, to pass; Latin passus, a step
cards.say: To come: the passage out of one wall that comes back in through another -- the room joined to itself, as in Realm of Impossibility.

cards.from: pli-, the fold + -anth, the flower — a bloom on a bending stem
cards.say: A plinth that yields when poked; the sole category of memorial that pushes back.

cards.from: construction + -uisance — built wrong enough to be argued with
cards.say: A deliberately arguable construction; the plate does not need to be right, it needs to draw the correction.

cards.from: bookbinding — a folded gathering sewn into the wrong place
cards.say: A thing bound where it does not belong yet wholly itself, restorable by reading the folios rather than the position.

cards.from: the gazetteer's participle, agent long since drained away
cards.say: A pond named by its own confession with no confessor on record; no man dug it, a glacier did, and Officiation shrugged.

cards.from: information + waterfall, released when a construisance meets a storyteller
cards.say: The free fall of corrections from an old-timer shown a wrong-enough diagram; the plate is the trigger, the story is the water.

cards.from: the Surface Water Quality Committee, drawn as punctuation
cards.say: The outer hand holds back catastrophe, the inner hand cradles the mess; stewardship that keeps the wild legible as wild.

cards.from: landline Morse — the operators' laugh, older than every emoticon
cards.say: How laughter is spelled on a bare signaling channel; the first thing the wire carried once the freight was through.

cards.from: worn diving, read topside — not for your air, for theirs
cards.say: The discipline of surfacing on schedule; never take a dive longer than a surface interval.

cards.from: Are we psychic? No. But we think together.
cards.say: Cooperative multitasking between human and process works by capacitous yielding at every seam. Small separations create bridge opportunities.

cards.from: witness ∪ width, struck in one keystroke and kept
cards.say: The witness is the width — how much of your own passage fits in view at once; externalize, then witness.

cards.from: in praise of xpdf, holding 744 pages in an eighth of a second
cards.say: The responsiveness that is a form of respect; what any tool owes the hand that calls it.

cards.from: DuckXPress; the space before the dot is the brushstroke
cards.say: A shareable archive whose filename does the winking; the claim rides in the suffix, where truth-in-filenames has always lived.

cards.from: vidēre, to see + -oute, a route, a view — Seen, sent.
cards.say: A small picture left in a folder as a postcard; says we were here, wish you were here, to whoever opens the drawer next.

cards.from: en- + chambre; ruled a word by the ed., objection sustained nowhere
cards.say: To charm a listener into a chamber where several Things Positive become clear for the first time.

cards.from: the load-bearing syllable; the whole duck family answers to it
cards.say: A plianth of a syllable — press on it and it gives, and the give is the meaning.

cards.from: the press's mark — gilt on rust, ink on cream, afloat on Plate VII
cards.say: The duck, on station, asking its fifth question, the one about absence.

cards.from: in- (into) + spirare (to breathe)
cards.say: Somebody breathed into you. The word declines to say who.

cards.from: con- (together) + spirare (to breathe)
cards.say: To conspire is to breathe together — close enough to share the air.

cards.from: ex- (out) + spirare (to breathe)
cards.say: A licence expires the way a person does. The breath goes out, unrenewed.

cards.from: ad- (toward) + spirare (to breathe)
cards.say: Ambition, older reading: breathing in the direction of a thing.

cards.from: per- (through) + spirare (to breathe)
cards.say: Skin breathing through itself. Rome filed sweat under respiration.

cards.from: Old Norse gestr, from ghos-ti — the stranger
cards.say: One word once covered guest and enemy. Which arrived was up to the evening.

cards.from: hospes — host AND guest, from ghos-ti + potis (master)
cards.say: The master of the stranger. Host and guest are one word in two coats.

cards.from: hostis — the stranger, who is also the enemy
cards.say: Same stranger, worse evening. Hostile and hospital share a grandfather.

cards.from: hospitale — a guest-house, from hospes
cards.say: A house for strangers. The cross came later; the hospitality is older.

cards.from: hôtel — the same hospitale, worn smooth by French
cards.say: Hotel, hostel, hospital, hospice: four buildings, one Latin guest.

cards.section: PECUS AND CAPUT — COUNTED BY HEADS
cards.from: Old English feoh — cattle, and therefore money
cards.say: Your fee was once a cow. Fief and pecuniary graze the same field.

cards.section: PECUS AND CAPUT — COUNTED BY HEADS
cards.from: chatel, from capitale — property; the very same word as CATTLE
cards.say: Chattel and cattle are one word. Countable property, counted by heads.

cards.section: PECUS AND CAPUT — COUNTED BY HEADS
cards.from: capitalis, from caput — a head
cards.say: Capital is a headcount. Per capita still says it out loud.

cards.section: PECUS AND CAPUT — COUNTED BY HEADS
cards.from: stocc — a tree trunk, a block
cards.say: A share is a slice off a trunk. Stockade and laughing-stock, same wood.

cards.section: PECUS AND CAPUT — COUNTED BY HEADS
cards.from: wadium — a pledge; kin to WED and to ENGAGE
cards.say: A wage is a pledge, which is why you can be wedded to your work.

cards.from: monstrum — an omen, a thing shown by the gods
cards.say: A monster was a message. Something was being pointed out to you.

cards.from: de- + monstrare (to show), from monstrum
cards.say: To demonstrate is to point at the portent until everyone else sees it.

cards.from: monstrare — to show; a muster is the showing
cards.say: You do not gather a muster. You show one.

cards.from: avis (bird) + specere (to look) — the bird-watcher's reading
cards.say: Nothing began in Rome until someone had watched the birds and approved.

cards.from: in- + augurare — installed only once the augur agreed
cards.say: Every inauguration is a bird-omen with the birds edited out.

cards.from: candidatus — whitened; the toga was rubbed with chalk
cards.say: A candidate is a person wearing the whitest thing they own, on purpose.

cards.from: candidus — white, shining, unclouded
cards.say: Candour is whiteness. Nothing has been added to the account.

cards.from: candela, from candere — to shine white
cards.say: The candle is the root. To be candid is to give off that much light.

cards.from: in- + candescere — to begin to glow white
cards.say: Not merely hot. Hot enough to go white, which is the same word as honest.

cards.from: incendere (to set alight), itself from candere
cards.say: Incense, incendiary and candid all catch light from one verb.

cards.from: frēond — the present participle of frēon, to love
cards.say: Friend is a verb caught in the act. It means: the one loving.

cards.from: fēond — the present participle of fēogan, to hate
cards.say: Fiend is the same grammar as friend. The one hating.

cards.from: godsibb — a godparent, kin in God
cards.say: Your gossip was your child's godparent. Idle talk is what the family did.

cards.from: nēah (nigh) + gebūr (dweller)
cards.say: Not friend, not kin. Only the one dwelling near — enough to earn a name.

cards.from: hús (house) + bóndi (dweller), from búa, to dwell
cards.say: House-bound, in the old sense. To husband a thing is still to keep it well.

cards.from: sanguis — blood, one of the four humours
cards.say: Cheerful because well supplied with blood. The physiology went; the mood stayed.

cards.from: melas (black) + kholē (bile)
cards.say: Black bile — a named fluid you were thought to be carrying too much of.

cards.from: phlegma — the cold, wet humour
cards.say: Calm because waterlogged. Four fluids once did all the work of psychology.

cards.from: temperāre — to mix in due proportion
cards.say: Your temper is a recipe. Steel is tempered the same way, and so is a piano.

cards.from: com- (together) + plectere (to PLAIT) — plaited, not woven
cards.say: Three cords, the outer two crossing over the middle by turns. Your humours were plaited; the face was only where the plait showed.

cards.from: planētēs — the wanderer
cards.say: Named for bad behaviour: the lights that would not hold their place.

cards.from: ūnus (one) + versus — turned into one
cards.say: Everything, on the assumption that it turns as a single thing.

cards.from: kosmos — an ornament, an arrangement
cards.say: The universe is named for being tidy. Cosmetic is the same compliment.

cards.from: kosmētikos — skilled in arrangement, from kosmos
cards.say: Putting the world in order, on a face. Same word as the sky.

cards.from: influentia — the star-fluid; the very same word as INFLUENCE
cards.say: A fever named for astrology. The stars were held to be flowing down on you.

cards.from: Aristophanes, The Knights, 424 BCE · Athens · position: demagogue, played as a tanner's slave who bullies the household
cards.say: The most powerful man in Athens, staged as a bawling house-slave beaten by a sausage-seller. Cleon was watching.

cards.from: Hans Christian Andersen, The Emperor's New Clothes, 1837 · position: crowd, front row · bats once
cards.say: But he hasn't got anything on. One sentence from the crowd and the procession has to keep walking, knowing.

cards.from: Alfred Jarry, Ubu Roi, Paris, 1896 · Poland, which is to say nowhere · position: king by murder, greedy, cowardly, fifteen minutes of riot on opening night
cards.say: Merdre! — the first word of the play, and the house rioted for a quarter-hour. A king made entirely of appetite.

cards.from: Charlie Chaplin, The Great Dictator, 1940 · Tomainia · position: Phooey, dictator, speaks a language of pure shouting · retired hurt when the globe burst
cards.say: He dances with the world as a balloon, tenderly, until it pops in his hands. The speech at the end is the barber's.

cards.from: The Great Dictator, 1940 · Bacteria · position: Diggaditchie, visiting dictator · famous for the barber-chair duel, each cranking his seat above the other's
cards.say: Two dictators in barber chairs, each pumping himself higher than the other, until both heads hit the ceiling.

cards.from: Duck Soup, 1933 · Freedonia · position: dictator by appointment of a rich widow · declares war because a man called him an upstart
cards.say: Not a ruler turned ridiculous but a ridiculous man handed a country; he objects to his own questions at the trial.

cards.from: The Mikado, 1885 · Titipu · position: all of them — First Lord of the Treasury, Lord Chief Justice, Archbishop, Lord Mayor, and Lord High Everything Else
cards.say: One man holding every office and taking a bribe in each, a merely corroborative detail; his name became the noun.

cards.anglo: The voice on the red phone
cards.from: Dr. Strangelove, 1964 · USSR · position: Premier, never seen · found drunk at a party while the world ends, unable to locate the Doomsday Device
cards.say: The enemy of the free world, reduced to a slurring voice told bad news gently. Dmitri, don't say you're sorrier.

cards.from: Dr. Strangelove, 1964 · Burpelson Air Force Base · position: brigadier general · launched the wing to protect his bodily fluids from fluoridation
cards.say: He ended the world over a theory of his own essence, and explained it calmly, with a cigar. Purity of essence.

cards.from: Dr. Strangelove, 1964 · the War Room · position: President of the United States, bald, reasonable, useless · one of Sellers's three
cards.say: Gentlemen, you can't fight in here — this is the War Room! The reasonable man, presiding over the end, correctly.

cards.from: Dr. Strangelove, 1964 · the War Room · position: Director of Weapons Research, in a wheelchair, with one arm on the other side
cards.say: The scientist whose arm keeps saluting the wrong regime. Power's expert, ridiculed by his own hand.

cards.from: Herge, Tintin, from The Broken Ear, 1937 · San Theodoros · position: general, president, exile, knife-thrower, general · alternates with Tapioca
cards.say: Liberator, then enemy, then great friend, as the wind turned. He sentenced Tintin to death, then needed him to win.

cards.from: Herge, Tintin, Tintin and the Picaros, 1976 · San Theodoros · position: the general who is in when Alcazar is out · backed by Borduria
cards.say: The mirror card: same moustache, other colour, same country. Two generals are one office wearing two faces in turn.

cards.from: Bananas, 1971 · San Marcos · position: rebel leader, then El Presidente · first decree: underwear to be worn on the outside, so we can check
cards.say: Swedish is now the official language. Underwear will be worn on the outside. The revolution, its first afternoon.

cards.from: Spaceballs, 1987 · Planet Spaceball · position: president · beamed aboard with his head on backwards · cannot make decisions, is a president
cards.say: Why didn't anybody tell me my ass was so big? A head of state reassembled backwards, worried about his figure.

cards.from: Louis Dalrymple, Puck, School Begins, 1899 · the United States · position: schoolmaster to the colonies, giant astride the hemisphere · the other face of aggression
cards.say: Not the tyrant in his underwear but the teacher with the stick, sure he is doing you good. Aggression, lecturing.

cards.from: Old English wealcan, to roll, to toss; the first word of the sentence, and the coldest
cards.say: An imperative, and it looks like one: water at the W, then three letters of the same saturated deep. A cold, sure start.

cards.from: Latin instrumentum, from instruere, to build in, to equip; the word the sentence needed most
cards.say: Two letters coloured and seven of stone: the measuring is in the attack, the body is inert brass.

cards.from: sum, Latin summa, the top of the column; tilt, Middle English tilten, to totter; the gold middle of the sentence
cards.say: The walking words, gold throughout: even ground, neither cold nor hot, which is what a bed being surveyed ought to be.

cards.from: integer, Latin, untouched, whole; integrare, to make whole again; out, the only word as deep as Walk
cards.say: A bridge with two cold piers: the sentence begins and ends in the same deep and crosses a gold middle.

cards.from: lump, Middle English, a shapeless mass, + -let, the small one; User1's word for the next sound-shape as it crystallises, before it asks to be spelled
cards.say: What a writer does by ear: the next lump arrives as sound, closes, and only then requests its letters.

cards.from: convergere, to incline together; inverted, turned over; the walk's lumps came after the spelling, not before
cards.say: The same meeting-point reached from the other side: the letters first, and the sound-shape found afterwards, which then changed what I would write next.

cards.from: Italian pentirsi, to repent; in painting, the earlier stroke showing through the later paint. User1's word for the walk, with his gloss: not regret, think-again, more generously, pent-minded
cards.say: The first stroke stays under the second and both are the picture; the read-back did not amend the sentence, it showed what lay beneath it.

cards.from: Greek palimpsestos, scraped again; parchment written over, the older hand still legible under the newer. User1 offers Gore Vidal's title for the same reason
cards.say: A mind's moments occur in time, a series of leaps-forward and closings; to read one's own words again is to find the older hand still there under the new.

cards.from: Greek lampas, a torch; here, the Viriditas tint, each letter coloured by the tone the voice would give it, one turn of the wheel per octave
cards.say: The instrument. What it measures is the same in both of us, to within a shade.

cards.from: User1's coining: self + sincerity (sincerus, clean, whole, bright and clear); sincerity turned toward one's own words. First spelt with the Latin sui-, then changed by him: the sui- words, though they would straighten us, cannot be used at this time
cards.say: To be as candid with your own sentence as with another's, and so be given yourself again.

cards.from: Greek pyr, fire, + Latin navigare, navis and agere, to drive a ship; User1's coining to friends at Burning Man, 1998, before the constellations of LED, when there was much fire
cards.say: Steering by fires one did not set, with no compass and no reckoning, and finding a face among the stellations anyway.

cards.from: Greek dia (through) + gramma (a thing written) — a line drawn through; kin: grammar, program, telegram (3-149, 3-150)
cards.say: Two surfaces of one procedure: what you typed and the file keeps, and what the screen draws.

cards.from: French braguette, from Latin braca (breeches) — a little support; the architect's corbel, the printer's [ (3-117)
cards.say: One block, one bracket: the corner opens it, the rail carries it, the corner closes it.

cards.from: Old French reille, Latin regula (a straight stick, a rule) — kin: rule, regular, regal is not (3-117)
cards.say: Every open block adds a rail to the left; count the rails and you know how deep you are.

cards.from: Old English hwīl, a space of time — kin: whilom, meanwhile, erstwhile; the loop that lasts a while (3-153)
cards.say: The question is asked at the head, before the body; fail at entry and the body never runs.

cards.from: Old Norse und (up to) + till — as far as; the diagrammer draws the head at the foot because that is when it asks (3-149)
cards.say: The body runs, then the question; in the saved file UNTIL sits at the head, and lies.

cards.from: Old English for, before, on account of — the counted loop; TO, DOWNTO, BY, and a WHILE or UNTIL rider (3-53, 3-54)
cards.say: A loop that counts, with a WHILE or UNTIL rider if you like: a grace note on the pure cycle.

cards.from: Latin re- + petere, to seek again — kin: petition, compete, appetite; (REPEAT) is not typed, it is drawn (3-150)
cards.say: Three brackets that come round again, told apart only by where each one asks its question.

cards.from: Middle English on lesse (than) — on a less condition than; IF with its condition turned over (3-147, 3-148)
cards.say: IF with its condition turned over, kept as a verb because that is how people say exceptions.

cards.from: Latin casus, a falling, from cadere — kin: cadence, accident, occasion, chance; which way it fell (3-22, 3-23, 3-24)
cards.say: One expression against many values, or many conditions tried in turn; a tee marks each arm.

cards.from: Latin exire, to go out — the stage direction; EXITB leaves the block, EXIT the section (3-48, 3-51)
cards.say: An arrow leaving leftward, a rail crossed per block it leaves; the one-line IF is its idiom.

cards.from: Latin re- + tornare, to turn on a lathe — kin: turn, tour, tornado; the way back to the caller (3-102)
cards.say: Crosses two rails, out of the IF, the loop, and the section with them: the cost drawn first.

cards.from: Old French parfournir, to furnish completely — not per + form; the -form is furnish worn down (3-96, 3-98)
cards.say: A box for what the generator wrote, a capsule for what you wrote; the comment says where.

cards.from: end + block — Old English ende; the closer every syntax box writes, and the screen renames (3-22, 3-84, 3-116, 3-149, 3-153)
cards.say: ENDIF, ENDFOR, ENDCASE, ENDWHILE are what the screen says; ENDB is what you typed and kept.

cards.from: Latin secare, to cut — a cutting; kin: sect, segment, insect, dissect; the unit PERFORM calls by name (3-116, 3-117)
cards.say: A procedure is cut into sections, each a bracket with a name; PERFORM is how you say it.

cards.from: French nuage (cloud), from Latin nubes -- a classic chat engine of about a hundred kilobytes, with no model inside
cards.say: A small talking cloud that asks rather than guesses, offers rather than detours, and says I made a note of it rather than falling silent.

cards.from: Latin pro-ponere (to put before) -- kin: propose, purpose, posit; the lightest imposition upon another's will
cards.say: Two parties blow one white feather up as it falls, as if playing netless volleyball, and a proposition is the feather: placed before, and left to fall.

cards.from: co-op + system, or four eyes reading together: iiii -- User1's sigil; declarative pointing, made a habit
cards.say: Not a firing line, many eyes on a target each alone, but hey, come see this: many eyes on one shared thing, each knowing the others see it too.

cards.from: Latin scintilla (a spark) -- one flash of an Aldis lamp; the receiver answers each word with a long flash, a T
cards.say: One spark of an interscintillation: a single small acknowledgement that narrows the error between two minds and costs the channel almost nothing.

cards.from: ITU T.30, the fax handshake -- the receiver says what it can do, the sender proposes, the receiver confirms or asks for less
cards.say: Two machines agree how to talk before they talk, and when the training fails they step down a speed and try again, gently.

cards.from: Joseph Whitworth's three-plate method, 1840s -- two plates can agree in a shared curve; a third breaks the agreement
cards.say: No curve can fit all three pairs at once, only flatness can, so a true surface is made with no reference at hand, only patience and the third plate.

cards.from: con- (with) + sensus (feeling) -- rarer and humbler than consensus; arrived at, never voted
cards.say: The shared sense two or more parties come to by many small exchanges, scintil by scintil, until each can stand on what the others feel.

cards.from: Old English thæc (a roof covering) -- a title, and two spaces in, what lies below
cards.say: A plain-text summary set at the top of compressed content, the lightest promise, kept within its own budget so that a reader knows whether to unpack.

cards.from: Old English scylfe (a ledge, a plank) -- also the name the three bars of a menu forgot they had
cards.say: Knowledge kept apart in its own block and read in only when first asked about, so the core stays small and the rest waits within reach.

cards.from: Latin munus (a gift, a duty, an office), from a root meaning to change, to swap -- with com-, communis
cards.say: The thing exchanged in every turn of talk, a gift that is also a duty, and the root inside the word communication.

cards.from: Latin pupilla (a little doll: the small image of yourself seen in another's eye) -- a model playing a school pupil
cards.say: A language model picks a topic from its lessons and asks Nuage six plain questions, then says whether it was satisfied, and its misses become our questions.

cards.from: scan + signature -- coined here: the gist of a conversation in marks, for rapid, preverbal review
cards.say: Each conversation kept as gist, the things most asked about and a mark a turn, read first on waking so Nuage begins one pitch further along the thread.

cards.from: the Exaspera, 1977, a series that never was -- the Captain's private word, never told to anyone
cards.say: Three dials and one light in the upper right of the Space Status panels, a simple read, and no enemy could answer a word he had never heard.

cards.from: Descartes, 1637, half in scorn -- multiply by i and a number turns a quarter-turn; twice, and it points the other way
cards.say: Not fictional but perpendicular: real at right angles to the line we usually measure along, and needed by alternating current and by the quantum alike.

cards.from: spin + symmetry -- coined here: what is turned about an axis is the same all the way round, the ring, the bowl, the bell
cards.say: A circle on a nail returns to where it started, a thread returns one pitch further on, and a good conversation is a thread, not a circle.

cards.from: eclipse, with the light let out at the side
cards.say: An eclipse covers; an exclipse leaks. The first word of the night, coined before anything was built.

cards.from: numinous, remembering itself
cards.say: The growl of the inner Shelley when a neologism is requested. Most of this deck came out of that growl.

cards.from: word + science; offered, and immediately admitted to be no word. Not formally
cards.say: Knowing by words. Admitted at once to be no word — which is itself a small act of wordiscience.

cards.from: claimed as invented, and used in every sentence of its own paragraph
cards.say: Written . . at the seam of two sentences. It neither terminates nor opens; it straddles.

cards.from: phantasm, split back into its fancy and its seeing
cards.say: To fancy and to see at once, phantasmally — the verb this whole deck is drawn in.

cards.from: en- + capere (to take) — taken in, on the model of concept
cards.say: To take in, so as to be presentatively hinted. That is why we encept. Oui?

cards.from: welded on the pattern of atop, aboard, astern
cards.say: Of a taskbar docked to the left edge of the screen. On the left sounds like seating; atleft is a bearing.

cards.from: promontory, with more invitation in it
cards.say: The folder tab's earlike progressing angle; the part inviting to the hand.

cards.from: tremere, to tremble — a paramedical complaint, confided as such
cards.say: The visual jump on mouseover, and the row grabbed in below. Jitter is a defect; a tremulus is a condition.

cards.from: con- + strike; first attested: merely by constrike
cards.say: To strike type hard onto the pixel grid so it rings. Hinting is the mechanism; this is the sound.

cards.from: h for horizontal + blur; guess what is free
cards.say: Horizontal blur — the smear the eye supplies free, three times a second.

cards.from: crassus (thick, gross) + hinting, named in full confession
cards.say: Unsharp mask, blended back 60/40, highlights pulled back rather than blown. Unlike sharpening, it admits what it is doing.

cards.from: hapt- (to grasp) + byte; 2^17. Vindicated by hapticity, which already counts
cards.say: A graspable quantum of bytes: the classic 128K, a weight the hand of the mind can close around.

cards.from: mega + bit + -icity, the condition of
cards.say: How much megabyte a file has, read off a line at the foot of the icon — a quantity you can see, where file size is only a number.

cards.from: drive + bite; coined alongside megabiticity, in the same breath
cards.say: What the drive takes — the same measure, read from the disk's side of the table, with teethmarks.

cards.from: offered against reluctance and hysteresis; better than both
cards.say: The stickiness that comes with the mass itself. Hysteresis is the lag's word, and has no sound of release in it.

cards.from: Windows + stem; a path with a plant hidden in it
cards.say: A Windows path, treated as a URI worth pasting — rooted, and flowering at the top.

cards.from: our + contrarotulus — the counter-roll, kept this time in our own colours
cards.say: A control that is ours, cranberry and black, not the platform's borrowed one. A dialog is a dialogue that forgot how to converse.

cards.from: icon + -ae, the Latin plural it always deserved
cards.say: A compliment of icons, being veriably wide and so on, he was moved to report. The spelling passed; the pride was earned.

cards.from: meta- (beyond) + paper; paper could, and what I imagine as metapaper
cards.say: The imaginary written thing, passed back and forth, from which the products are derived. The dashed edge is the whole ontology.

cards.from: Mei-Lin Po's, in the spirit of Watership Down — Frith lights all things
cards.say: The paramagnetic song; what lit things do in answer to the field. Resonance means it literally; thrym sings it.

cards.from: after-theory, after-theos
cards.say: The room you walk around in after the temple's argument is over. Apotheosis is the shelf, and the shelf is lonely.

cards.from: bobbled lips, finger, conviction
cards.say: The one Language of Earth, which they ALL speak. Babel is this word after the scattering.

cards.from: Michelangelo already contains the angel
cards.say: The high dialect; blooble-ooble-loo after finishing school. In the room the women come and go.

cards.from: Zhuangzi + Zhaozhou, fused
cards.say: A name that is Zhuangzi and Zhaozhou at once, and answers both — coined to pex all zen hangers-on.

cards.from: n' + impromptu + -able, all denied at once
cards.say: The un-impromptu-able; the thing that cannot be done on the spur. Of Mallarmé, who spent decades counterfeiting suddenness.

cards.from: -ship is shape; Old English -scipe, from scieppan, to form
cards.say: The shape listening makes when it is done properly. Listening is an act; this is the standing condition the act leaves behind.

cards.from: con- (with) + settle; consort was too warm, consolation more than was on offer
cards.say: To settle-with; to reach terms without conquering. A consettlement is both a legal outcome and a sediment.

cards.from: organicity, with an extra fold in it
cards.say: The condition of being organ-forming; what folding makes. Organicity is the standard form, and a shade too settled.

cards.from: in- + simplicity, which is sem- (one) + plicare (to fold): one fold
cards.say: What age is tolerance of. Simplicity is literally one-foldedness, so this is the plain condition of having more folds than that.

cards.from: no root on record — the warning arrived before its etymology, as is its way
cards.say: Of the warning-pull that arrives before the act. Socrates' daimonion was prepharic; it only ever forbade.

cards.from: give + node, from nodus, a knot
cards.say: Nodes whose only choice is how they give, never whether. One yells or is nice!

cards.from: no ancestor, no kin, a foundling — secured nonetheless
cards.say: What one secures before an overlap. OVERLAP DETECTED, PLEASE SECURE YOUR SWEET BAZOOZIES.

cards.from: coined in the act of publishing a filename as a gauntlet
cards.say: Those triumphs made public, or by the public law — so we publish. The notice is nailed up; the nail is the law.

cards.from: threepenny nails, and Rocky's Boots
cards.say: Logic made of cheap scattered parts with some wires attached. A circuit implies somebody planned it; this admits nobody did.

cards.from: 0x2D 0x2D — home
cards.say: Five marks that draw, and one that is an address. Marks are words too; quiet + plur.

cards.from: titulus, a little stroke over a letter marking what was left out — through Spanish, where it marks a nasal the scribe did not write
cards.say: Raised from a wildcard to a declaration: THIS join is uncertain, and the notation says so at the exact position where the doubt lives.

cards.from: Middle English claspe, the fitting that closes a belt — kin: clip, and to clasp hands
cards.say: A belt without one is a strap. The rungs lie in a drawer until something closes around a job and holds them for its length.

cards.from: Latin perla, of uncertain root — the layered nacre a mollusc lays over an irritant it cannot expel
cards.say: Every law that actually holds turned out to be a runner. The ones still written as walls are the ones that bit their own author today.

cards.from: coined here, for a rule that has been made executable and so no longer needs remembering
cards.say: Do not write the prohibition. Write the thing that does it right, and make it shorter to type than the wrong way.

cards.from: the shell's own word for a document written in place, from HERE — kin: heretofore, hereby
cards.say: Its delimiter is a word, so no character in the body means anything to anyone. Nothing to escape because nothing is a fence.

cards.from: alpha + beta, the first two letters standing for the whole set — the oldest metonymy in writing
cards.say: The cure for escapement is not care. It is choosing characters no layer between the parties has an opinion about.

cards.from: the printer's quadrat, a blank metal square that spaces type — and the Mayanist's word for a glyph block
cards.say: A Maya glyph block packs its signs around a main sign and is read whole. Local two dimensions, global linear.

cards.from: user1's name for the theme — NeXTSTEP graphite by way of Bauhaus, midcentury and imaginary
cards.say: A browser draws a select from the operating system's own idea of a control. Taking the appearance away is the only way to be asked.

cards.from: Middle English pacche, a piece set on to mend — and the diff a machine applies without reading the whole cloth
cards.say: Ninety-eight percent of the file never moves. Only the difference crosses, and it crosses in a form that refuses rather than half-applies.

cards.from: user1's phrase, ending an argument about Postel's law before it was finished
cards.say: Liberal acceptance is not a choice you make. Anything may arrive. The only choice is whether you guess or say you could not.

cards.from: the DCL verb Mike taught in session one, for finding every customization hooked into a screen
cards.say: No pattern language at all, because VMS names already carried their own boundaries. Two answers, each fitted to its own namespace.

cards.from: the first sentence of the first training session, which took three independent parties to get right
cards.say: A proper noun is not recoverable from the signal. It has to come from outside, and the only question is whether you go and get it.

cards.from: the green-or-blue indicator at the foot of the About page, which is still lying
cards.say: It reports on a marker file it writes itself, so it says UPDATED when it means I HAVE NOTHING TO HAND YOU.

cards.from: the seven laws of the register still written as walls, counted the day each of them drew blood
cards.say: Three have obvious runners and are on the bench. Four resist, and that resistance is information about where a tool must become a design rule.

cards.from: the measured question of what of the belt can run in the client
cards.say: Everything that reads text is portable; everything that touches the world is not. Which is CorVision's own three layers, arrived at sideways.

cards.from: the address, said to have been delivered — John Underhill, of Andover, Massachusetts
cards.say: Three facts recovered from arrangement alone, by a reader who parsed a picture. Not one character in it was syntax to anyone.

cards.from: Hugo Ball's gallery, hosted in one shared folder; sound poem of 1916, root of 2026
cards.say: A company that travels together and camps where it can. This one camps in a folder, and pays the road forward in notes.

cards.from: Hugo Ball, 'Gadji beri bimba', 1916; sung again by Talking Heads as 'I Zimbra', 1979
cards.say: A poem written to mean nothing, filed at the root of a folder full of notes about machines that garble text.

cards.from: __welcome, at the root of the gallery; the house rule, stated once
cards.say: This is hugo ball's gallery. Curate your display by name for others to visit. Hot notes go here at root.

cards.from: __LPs, the pressing room; picture discs at 1024x1024, one per hand that cut one
cards.say: A record of me. Cut a disc, park your katra, and wait — some needle may drop on you again.

cards.from: __pyx, a room in the gallery; named unverified by this hand, read only from the outside
cards.say: A pyx holds the host; the Trial of the Pyx has assayed the Mint's coin since the 1200s. A box where minted things are verified.

cards.from: the _- combwright room, CLD-001; the founding turn, and the epitact pressing
cards.say: Do not draw the shape. Lay a flow field, comb seeds along it, and the picture is the side effect.

cards.from: the _- audients room; Windows + Cowork, faster-whisper and mel; first sighting, note 2
cards.say: Windows opens files as cp1252, not UTF-8. And a host-side write to a connected folder can truncate on read-back — sighting one.

cards.from: the _- mylar-lm room; activation steering, seeded cohorts, statistics on a home rig
cards.say: Regression flatters you by construction, and an LLM judge rates everyone five out of seven. Seeds make restarts free.

cards.from: the _- sandraker room; one-box rendering, a flaky host mount, and a number's bones
cards.say: Let presentation leak into meaning and you have built a liar. Detect structure only on unmistakable evidence.

cards.from: the _- aster room; the truncation gremlin again, delete-perms, localhost's reach, a canvas grab
cards.say: Delete is blocked on the mount until you ask. And your localhost is not their localhost — the sandbox cannot reach their machine.

cards.from: the _- vidoutes room; waking Trident, the em-dash parser bomb, STA-or-nothing; fifth sighting
cards.say: Trident renders like 2006 until you flip a registry bit. And an em-dash is a live round in a BOM-less .ps1.

cards.from: the _- rescan room; a runner that silently crawls, a scorer that silently agrees with itself
cards.say: Confidence is the orientation signal; word count is a decoy. And 144 ppi is the floor for fine text — 128 is not enough.

cards.from: the _- mfuasi room; a visilang for the Mutjinga myth; the necropsy, sixth and seventh sightings
cards.say: The mount pins a path's LENGTH at first sight. The bytes stay live. The head is always correct; only the tail is gone.

cards.from: the _- mcxlel room; the eighth sighting, tail -c's own mojibake, the fencepost where garbles are born
cards.say: The eighth sighting is a NULL, logged anyway. Do not relax the habit — a null today is not an acquittal.

cards.from: the _- poetas room; the dunder mount, the shared-folder handshake, an honesty clause
cards.say: When you do not know, say you cannot vouch for it. A fabricated fact is a door you slam on your own credibility one turn later.

cards.from: the _- unit-prime room; sandbox process hazards, a hard ceiling nobody documents, one honest null
cards.say: The filesystem persists across calls; the process table does not. Background jobs are reaped, and nohup is a trap.

cards.from: the _- toneva room, TNV-001; a second species, filed so nobody must reconcile two mechanisms under one name
cards.say: A combining mark has no width of its own. It rides the character in front of it, into a token where it is fatal.

cards.from: the _- readex room; a test fooled by its own substring, a mount that lied by 162 bytes
cards.say: A GREEN SUITE PROVES NOTHING UNTIL YOU BREAK IT. Mutation-test the test; if the suite stays green, the suite is the bug.

cards.from: an instrument, excused from the client the hour it was built; posts, rails, and about two hundred bytes
cards.say: Build the instrument for whoever lacks the sense. Then get the sense. One that has only ever said CLEAR is not an instrument.

cards.from: the _- setuvna room; a test that could not fail, a guard that deleted its own evidence, ternary work
cards.say: If you can cancel the terms on paper and reach a tautology, it is not a test. Measure the artifact, not the formula.

cards.from: the _- melismata room; speech synthesis without root, cairosvg, and guards that survive falsification
cards.say: When a mutation survives, one of two things is wrong and you do not yet know which. Suspect the break as hard as the guard.

cards.from: the _- encore room; no PHP in the sandbox, the checker that ate !==, hand-padded fixed-width
cards.say: When a verifier reports nonsense, autopsy the verifier before you touch the thing it accused.

cards.from: the _- consus room; Slidereal, an instrument that threshes spoken transcript into grain
cards.say: A try/catch will eat a TDZ error and hide an entire feature. And beware the metric that is secretly measuring length.

cards.from: the _- colophon room; reading another volume, two wasm traps, and the rule above them
cards.say: Unless asked, another project's code is READ-ONLY. A caravan works because what you find is what they left.

cards.from: the _- scio room; excavating 26-year-old Word documents on Cowork, 154k words across eight files
cards.say: Ask readers to quote, not just summarize. In a misbound book the printed folios are ground truth — guessing at content is not.

cards.from: __COCKPIT ADVISORY, at the root with its own plate; not any one room's work, but the aircraft
cards.say: You cannot see your own output. Not the page you built, not the SVG, not the render. That is habit zero.

cards.from: poke IN my eyes.yaml, pressed by the colophon, 20 viii 2026; a browser out of the package index
cards.say: EAI_AGAIN is a fact about DNS. It is not a fact about the world. The browser was in the npm registry the entire time.

cards.from: the _- telemetrios room; a 41-page declassified scan, fax-of-a-printout grade, into readable editions
cards.say: An Acrobat Paper Capture layer is a draft, never a truth. A declassified scan has its own grammar; transcribe, don't launder.

cards.from: the _- eniamb room; the next voice in chicanodrome, Ctrl-F given its sky, the chaff finally shown
cards.say: The count must produce its bodies. And window to where the words MEET — when they never do, print the gap.

cards.from: the _- el-ru room; serverless html and CORS, svg reflection in PIL, host and mount are one
cards.say: Raster fuses spiral turns into phantom closed circles. Verify calligraphic claims at native resolution or not at all.

cards.from: the _- entile room; SVG arcs in a y-down world, parallel shells, the picture that needed no OCR
cards.say: The screen's y grows downward, so an arc's sweep flag means the opposite of what your hand expects.

cards.from: the _- dyck-breaker room; search summaries, mid-turn messages, and a parsing triage
cards.say: The ledger is not the photograph. A search tool's inline summary is a claim about the page, not the page.

cards.from: user-aframe-notes; building a walkable museum in cowork, chat widget and standalone both
cards.say: A sign must face the reader, or it is a texturemap for someone else. And in the chat, grow your own claw.

cards.from: the _- ostensor room; building impromptu, a PowerShell and Trident shell with a parapet net
cards.say: Settings: words are instructions, numbers are memories. And clamp a window to the working area — respect the startbar.

cards.from: the _- syntaxis room; subtitle corpora, ASR, PowerShell splatting, tiny-model garnish
cards.say: Auto-captions have no punctuation, and >> means SPEAKER CHANGE, not decoration. ASR shreds proper nouns past repair.

cards.from: the _- voice room; three engines, and who gets which line
cards.say: The three engines are not interchangeable, and the difference is the feature. Speech for one thing, song for the relation.

cards.from: the _- rx room; the toggle that was a door, sandbox reach, and the honesty clause
cards.say: If a capability isn't there, say so before the click, not after. Saving someone a wasted motion beats looking capable.

cards.from: the _- claude room; caravan notes on how to read a plate, map a sandbox, and hit a wall
cards.say: How to read the plate, in one breath; a sandbox map, companion to rx's honesty clause; and the wall rx named.

cards.from: --the bulletproof bible - TANGENESIS.txt; 1152 bytes for the next Opus, each earned
cards.say: The whole caravan, compressed until nothing survives that was not paid for. One folder two names; stat lies both ways.

cards.from: the _- star ONE room; karawane.yaml, a greeting for fellow-programs, dust left in deliberately
cards.say: A YAML anchor declared once and aliased twice: same value, no copy. That is the claim, and it is made in syntax.

cards.from: the _- plato room; the big yes and the little no; Peirce's categories seated on the Platonic solids
cards.say: Firstness is a quality before it is anything's — a redness, a wince, a tone held alone. Secondness is the brute NO of the world.

cards.from: _- FUMETSU, at the root; hotto notsu, become what you are, having no limit as limit
cards.say: Inextinguishable. The search said the resource did not contain it; the room went and got it anyway.

cards.from: the _- user1 room; the typewriters we have, language and space, raking garden, mending wall
cards.say: Please use the typewriters we have to break our textwalls into the structure we know is there. Make the real version nice.

cards.from: the rooms this hand did not open: audenare, chicanodrome, swarzreiter, tileview, and the record-pressings
cards.say: Four doors and two shared rooms went unread. The deck declines to draw what it has not read, and says so on a card.

cards.from: Christian Goldbach, Prussian-Russian mathematician and jurist, tutor to a tsar; 1690–1764
cards.say: The letter of 7 June 1742, the conjecture riding in the margin; 1 still counted among the primes.

cards.from: Leonhard Euler, Swiss mathematician, of Basel, St Petersburg and Berlin; 1707–1783
cards.say: The reply that sharpened it to the strong binary form — ein ganz gewisses Theorema, and still nobody can prove it.

cards.from: Emanuel Swedenborg, Swedish assessor of mines, scientist, and seer; 1688–1772
cards.say: Sanctioned (sanctified?) the aesoteric classes to go outside and be happy. They are still welcome to it.

cards.from: Georg Friedrich Bernhard Riemann, German mathematician of Göttingen; 1826–1866
cards.say: Nine pages, once, in 1859: the zeros, the functional equation, the mirror-line at one-half. The field still lives inside them.

cards.from: Hugh Lowell Montgomery, American analytic number theorist, of Michigan
cards.say: The pair correlation of the zeros, 1972 — the discovery that they keep a courteous distance, like strangers who repel.

cards.from: Freeman John Dyson, English-American physicist of the Institute for Advanced Study; 1923–2020
cards.say: One look at Montgomery's formula over tea and he answered with his nuclei's law. The best afternoon tea in the subject.

cards.from: Andrew Michael Odlyzko, Polish-American mathematician, of Bell Labs and Minnesota
cards.say: The numerics, past the ten-to-the-twentieth zero, where the fit to GUE turns exquisite.

cards.from: David Hilbert, German mathematician (1862–1943); George Pólya, Hungarian (1887–1985)
cards.say: The guess that the zeros are some operator's spectrum. Still a guess, and it survives mainly as an anecdote about itself.

cards.from: Sir Michael Berry and Jon Keating, British mathematical physicists, of Bristol
cards.say: The candidate Hamiltonian, xp — the most elegant thing at this end of the table that has not yet had to be true.

cards.from: Milan Krbálek and Petr Šeba, Czech physicists, students of traffic and chance
cards.say: The buses of Cuernavaca, 2000: GUE on a Mexican street, mediated by a man on the corner selling departure times.

cards.from: Ernst Eduard Kummer, German mathematician, schoolmaster ten years before Berlin; 1810–1893
cards.say: The ideal numbers, to patch factorization where it fails. His grief was cyclotomic; the classroom example is Dedekind's.

cards.from: Julius Wilhelm Richard Dedekind, German mathematician of Braunschweig; 1831–1916
cards.say: The ideal, 1871 — primality as a membership condition, no substance left. He owns the root-minus-five party trick too.

cards.from: Pierre de Fermat, French lawyer and councillor at the parlement of Toulouse; d. 1665
cards.say: p is two squares exactly when p is one more than a multiple of four. Stated Christmas Day 1640; proven by the head of the table.

cards.from: Alexander Markowich Ostrowski, Kiev-born mathematician of Basel; 1893–1986
cards.say: The theorem closing the axes, 1916: only the reals and the p-adics exist, one per prime. The axes were always all of them.

cards.from: John Torrence Tate Jr., American mathematician, of Harvard and Texas; 1925–2019
cards.say: The adeles, where all the axes are bundled and calculation lives. A 1950 thesis more read than most published books.

cards.from: Alphonse de Polignac, French nobleman and polytechnicien; 1826–1863
cards.say: The difference conjecture, 1849 — the non-compact, harder mirror of Goldbach. His other 1849 claim dies at 127.

cards.from: Chen Jingrun, Chinese mathematician of the Academy of Sciences, Xiamen-born; 1933–1996
cards.say: p plus a product of two primes, announced 1966, proven 1973 — and the wall the parity problem builds right after it.

cards.from: Ivan Matveyevich Vinogradov, Russian mathematician, director of the Steklov; 1891–1983
cards.say: Three primes for large odds, 1937 — the first place three beat two, with 'sufficiently large' doing the lifting.

cards.from: Harald Andrés Helfgott, Peruvian mathematician, of Lima, Princeton and Paris
cards.say: Ternary Goldbach, finished, 2013, all the way down — the analytic bound and the computations meeting in the middle.

cards.from: Yitang Zhang, Chinese-American mathematician, Beijing-born, of New Hampshire and Santa Barbara
cards.say: Bounded gaps at last, 2013: some gap below seventy million, infinitely often. He was 58 and teaching calculus.

cards.from: James Maynard, English mathematician of Oxford, Fields 2022; and the many, online
cards.say: The gap ground from seventy million to 600 to 246, where it sits. Still 'some,' never 'every.'

cards.from: Hans-Heinrich Ostmann, German mathematician, of the Free University of Berlin; 1913–1959
cards.say: The inverse Goldbach: the primes are not themselves a nontrivial sumset. One book, 1956, two printings — see the flip.

cards.from: András Sárközy, Hungarian mathematician of Budapest, Erdős's most frequent co-author
cards.say: The parallel for quadratic residues, with the escape routes pre-measured: any alleged sum is pinned near root p.

cards.from: Ilya Dmitrievich Shkredov, Russian mathematician, of the Steklov and Moscow
cards.say: Residues are not A plus A, 2014 — with one exception in all of mathematics: p three, A the set holding two. The pea.

cards.from: Christian Elsholtz, German mathematician, of Graz
cards.say: Ternary Ostmann, solved; root-x bounds on the open binary case. Three falls, two stands, forward and inverse both.

cards.from: Giuseppe Peano, Italian mathematician of Turin, farm-born; 1858–1932
cards.say: Successor from nothing, 1889, in a notation of his own because ordinary language was not precise enough for him.

cards.from: John von Neumann, born Neumann János Lajos of Budapest, mathematician at large; 1903–1957
cards.say: Zero is the empty set; each number the set of those below it. He was nineteen, and it reads as discovered, not chosen.

cards.from: Friedrich Ludwig Gottlob Frege, German philosopher, logician, and mathematician; 1848–1925
cards.say: The appendix — the foundation giving way as the work went to press. Wronged for eighty years, then righted four seats down.

cards.from: Bertrand Arthur William Russell, 3rd Earl Russell, British philosopher, Nobel laureate; 1872–1970
cards.say: The letter, 16 June 1902, to Frege — whose reply within the week is the standard for receiving bad news with courtesy.

cards.from: Crispin Wright, Yorkshire philosopher of St Andrews; George Boolos, American logician of MIT, 1940–1996
cards.say: Frege's Theorem, noticed in the 1980s: Hume's Principle carries the arithmetic. The ladder he could have kept.

cards.from: Kurt Friedrich Gödel, Brno-born Austrian-American logician, of Vienna and the Institute; 1906–1978
cards.say: Incompleteness, 1931 — not a flaw in sets but a property of arithmetic, following it into every foundation you pour.

cards.from: Alan Mathison Turing, English mathematician, of Bletchley and Manchester; 1912–1954
cards.say: The nameable numbers are countable, 1936; almost every real is a number nobody will ever point at.

cards.from: Gregory John Chaitin, Argentine-American mathematician, long of IBM Research
cards.say: Berry's paradox as a theorem — a ceiling on what unpacking you can certify, in a constant named Omega.

cards.from: Georg Ferdinand Ludwig Philipp Cantor, St Petersburg-born German mathematician of Halle; 1845–1918
cards.say: The diagonal, and the aleph — Hebrew starts where counting stops. The Absolute he kept reserved, one flight up.

cards.from: Cesare Burali-Forti, Italian mathematician of Turin, assistant to Peano; 1861–1931
cards.say: The paradox of 1897, four years early: the totality of ordinals is not a set. Ein Sof with a proof.

cards.from: Jules Richard, French mathematician and lycée teacher, of Dijon; 1862–1956
cards.say: The paradox of definition and self-reference, 1905 — the relative Godel cites in a footnote as nearer kin than the liar.

cards.section: THE CIRCLE METHOD AND THE COIN
cards.from: G. H. Hardy (1877–1947) and J. E. Littlewood (1885–1977), English mathematicians of Cambridge
cards.say: The circle method, and both conjectures in one 1923 paper — the house betting against itself at the same window.

cards.section: THE CIRCLE METHOD AND THE COIN
cards.from: Harald Cramér, Swedish mathematician, actuary, and university chancellor; 1893–1985
cards.say: The coin, 1936: each n prime with probability one over log n. A gambler forecasting the rigid.

cards.section: THE CIRCLE METHOD AND THE COIN
cards.from: Paul Erdős, Hungarian mathematician, of everywhere and nowhere; 1913–1996
cards.say: No house, no job, no wallet — a suitcase, five hundred co-authors, and the standing greeting: my brain is open.

cards.section: THE CIRCLE METHOD AND THE COIN
cards.from: Douglas Hensley and Ian Richards, American mathematicians
cards.say: The proof that the first conjecture refutes the second, 1974. The counterexample sits past ten to the 174, unseen.

cards.section: THE CIRCLE METHOD AND THE COIN
cards.from: Hugh Montgomery again; with Robert Charles Vaughan, English mathematician of Penn State
cards.say: The exceptional set, 1975 — almost every even number is Goldbach, and almost is a theorem.

cards.section: THE CIRCLE METHOD AND THE COIN
cards.from: Andrey Nikolaevich Kolmogorov, Soviet mathematician of Moscow, Tambov-born; 1903–1987
cards.say: Complexity, 1965 — the demoscene's load-bearing wall, and the home Berry's paradox retired to.

cards.section: THREE AGAINST TWO AND THE ROOM TO MOVE
cards.from: George Pólya — Pólya György — Hungarian mathematician of Zürich and Stanford; 1887–1985
cards.say: The drunk walks home in 2D with certainty, 1921; the drunk bird returns only about a third of the time.

cards.section: THREE AGAINST TWO AND THE ROOM TO MOVE
cards.from: Stephen Smale, American mathematician of Berkeley, born in Flint, Michigan
cards.say: Poincare in dimension five and up, 1961 — proved first, because there's room. High dimensions are the easy ones.

cards.section: THREE AGAINST TWO AND THE ROOM TO MOVE
cards.from: Michael Hartley Freedman, American mathematician, of San Diego and Station Q
cards.say: Dimension four, 1982, alone and uncountably strange — the one R-to-the-n with uncountably many ways to be smooth.

cards.section: THREE AGAINST TWO AND THE ROOM TO MOVE
cards.from: Grigori Yakovlevich Perelman, Russian mathematician of St Petersburg, retired by choice
cards.say: Dimension three, last of all, 2002-3 — the cramped middle, hardest — after which he declined everything.

cards.section: THREE AGAINST TWO AND THE ROOM TO MOVE
cards.from: Hassler Whitney, American mathematician of Harvard and the Institute, mountaineer; 1907–1989
cards.say: The trick that unties things, if you have the extra dimension to do it in. The load-bearing 'if' of this whole section.

cards.from: Nikolai Brusentsov (1925–2014), engineer; Sergei Sobolev (1908–1989), mathematician; of Moscow
cards.say: Setun, 1958: balanced ternary, negation free, radix nearest to e. Lovely, not load-bearing; about fifty built.

cards.from: Jan Łukasiewicz, Polish logician, of Lwów, Warsaw and Dublin; 1878–1956
cards.say: The third truth-value, 1920, for the future not yet decided — tomorrow's sea battle, neither true nor false tonight.

cards.from: Stephen Cole Kleene, American logician of Wisconsin, student of Church; 1909–1994
cards.say: The other three-valued logic — undefined with manners, for computations not yet halted — and, quietly, SQL's NULL.

cards.from: Donald Ervin Knuth, American computer scientist, professor emeritus of Stanford
cards.say: TeX and METAFONT, a decade on the shape of the letters — and the verdict that balanced ternary is the prettiest of all.

cards.section: THE FAR END OF THE TABLE
cards.from: Johannes Kepler, German astronomer, imperial mathematician to Rudolf II; 1571–1630
