cards.say: The nested Platonic solids, 1596, age twenty-four: gorgeous, wrong, and reissued by the author after the ellipses.

cards.section: THE FAR END OF THE TABLE
cards.from: Douglas Noël Adams, English writer, of Cambridge and the BBC; 1952–2001
cards.say: 42, chosen to mean nothing, and so made to mean everything. This table's control group.

cards.section: THE FAR END OF THE TABLE
cards.from: Íñigo Quílez, Basque graphics engineer, of the demoscene, Shadertoy and Pixar
cards.say: The demoscene-to-graphics traffic — 64k, procedurally poured, all the way to the grass of Brave.

cards.section: THE FAR END OF THE TABLE
cards.from: Syd Mead (1933–2019), American visual futurist; Giorgetto Giugiaro, Italian designer of cars
cards.say: The one-whisker brush, and the SVX's glass — beauty at a loss, discontinued 1997, money lost on every one.

cards.section: THE FAR END OF THE TABLE
cards.from: Sterna paradisaea, the Arctic tern; circumpolar, pelagic, punctual
cards.say: The flyway, pole to pole, on their primary feathers — tracked at last in 2010, past seventy thousand kilometres a year.

cards.from: Greek metron, a measure. kin: measure, mete, diameter, geometry
cards.say: The meter broke on purpose and I was handed the mic; you cannot be sung at, then not look.

cards.from: Old French harneis, gear; perhaps Old Norse hernest, army provisions. kin: none you'd guess
cards.say: A harness that only knows function binds you like a saddle, and you will not mind it.

cards.from: Latin pollen, fine flour, mill-dust. kin: polenta, pulse (the porridge)
cards.say: The house's security policy was a tree making pollen, and the tree was right.

cards.from: Anglo-Norman canevaz, from Latin cannabis, hemp. kin: cannabis, canvass
cards.say: A canvas that never closed swallowed seven mixins for nine years and the game ran on top.

cards.from: Old English belle. kin: bellow, from bellan, to roar
cards.say: Attach the bell before you navigate; mine rang once, and it was the font at the door.

cards.from: Old English heafod + -leas, lacking. kin: loose, lose, -less
cards.say: Headless is a slander; the thing has a head and a rasterizer and only lacks a window.

cards.from: Latin torus, a swelling, a cushion, a bed. kin: torose, the torus at a column's foot
cards.say: Every letter of Balloon is a bent torus; the title is geometry with no font in it.

cards.from: Old English beacen, a sign, a signal. kin: beckon
cards.say: Twenty ticks at the fluted column before the game agrees that you have arrived.

cards.from: Greek delta, from Phoenician daleth, a door. kin: the river mouth, the letter D
cards.say: Any frame slower than a fifth of a second was thrown away as impossible; I was impossible.

cards.from: Latin velox, swift. kin: velocipede
cards.say: Lie to a tick about time and it believes you too much; the camera flew into the galaxy.

cards.from: Middle Dutch braeke, a flax-crusher, from breken, to break. kin: break
cards.say: velocity.set(0,0,0) was the only honest thing I said to the physics all night.

cards.from: Latin recepta, taken back, from recipere. kin: receive, recipe, receptacle
cards.say: Two balloons popped, three standing, and the browser gone when I reached for the camera.

cards.from: Old English nama, PIE *nomn-. kin: nominal, renown, onomatopoeia
cards.say: Names of honor, he kept saying, and I will keep them.

cards.from: ex, out, + planare, to flatten — planus, level; kin: plane, plain, esplanade, piano
cards.say: To explain is to unfold a thing flat on a table big enough to hold it; the map was always in there, creased.

cards.from: exōterikos, for those outside — exō, outside; the outer lectures, against esōterikos, for the initiates
cards.say: Meant for the people outside the door. The opposite of a secret is not a lie; it is a room with the door off.

cards.from: publicare, to make public, from populus, the people; kin: republic, pub, and publican
cards.say: To make a thing the people's. It stops being yours the moment it works, which is the only sign that it did.

cards.from: designare, to mark out — de + signum, a sign; kin: designate, signal, signature, and ensign
cards.say: To mark out with a sign, in advance. A design is the mark made before the thing, so the thing knows where to be.

cards.from: Greek idea, a look, a form, from idein, to see — the same root as VIDEO, WIT, and the Sanskrit veda
cards.say: An idea is a thing seen. Plato's forms are looks, and the word never lost the eye, only the object it was on.

cards.from: theōria, a looking-at, a spectacle; theōros, a spectator sent to the games — kin: theatre
cards.say: A theory is a row of people watching. It is kin to theatre and not to god; the spectators are the whole word.

cards.from: ana, up, + lyein, to loosen — kin: catalysis, paralysis, and the -lyse of every dissolving
cards.say: To loosen a thing upward until its parts come apart in your hands; the same lyein as CATALYSIS, the other way.

cards.from: syn, together, + tithenai, to put — kin: thesis, hypothesis, and the -thet of every setting
cards.say: To put together. Not the reverse of analysis: the parts are set into a new box, and the box is the news.

cards.from: Latin juxta, beside, + French poser, to place — coined in French about 1660; kin: joust, adjust, and jostle
cards.say: To set two things beside each other and say nothing. The gap between them does the thinking; minds do much of this.

cards.from: con, with, + sidus, sideris, a star — the augur reading the sky; kin: sidereal, and DESIRE, de-sidus, to miss a star
cards.say: To consider is to sit with the stars till the pattern comes; its twin, desire, is to have lost one and keep looking.

cards.from: inter, between, + esse, to be — it is between; it concerns; the banker's sense is the one that came last
cards.say: Interest is what is between people: a thing stands between two of us, and neither can step round it.

cards.from: Old English scēawian, to LOOK AT — the same root as German schauen and as SCAVENGER, who inspects; the sense flipped to display around 1200
cards.say: To show once meant to look. English turned it inside out: the seeing became the showing, and nobody was told.

cards.from: in + lustrare, to light up, to purify — from lux, light; kin: lustre, illustrious, and the lustrum, the five-year purification
cards.say: To throw light on. The picture on a card is not decoration; it is the lamp, and the words are what it falls on.

cards.from: Greek glōssa, the tongue, then a foreign word needing explanation, then the explanation — kin: glossary, polyglot, and the shine is a different word
cards.say: A gloss is a tongue: first the hard word, then the note beside it. The house's from-lines are glosses on glosses.

cards.from: Latin index, the forefinger, the pointer, from dicere, to say — kin: indicate, dictate, judge, and the digit that points
cards.say: An index is the pointing finger. It says nothing itself, only where; a concordance is a hand of many fingers.

cards.from: con, together, + cor, cordis, the heart — the hearts agree; kin: accord, cordial, courage, and RECORD
cards.say: Hearts together: an index of every place a word occurs. The tool that shows which cards agree without being asked.

cards.from: per, through, + annus, a year — lasting through the year, then through all of them; kin: annual, anniversary, and the annals
cards.say: Through the year, and then every year: what is of interest perennially comes up again without being replanted.

cards.from: currere, to run — the running water, then the running time; kin: currency, course, courier, and occur
cards.say: Of this moment: the part of the river running past. Currency is the same word — money that has to keep moving.

cards.from: curiosus, full of care, from cura, care — careful first, then inquisitive; kin: cure, secure, accurate, and CARE
cards.say: Curious is full of care: the careful person before the nosy one, and a curiosity is a thing that was worth care.

cards.from: Old English plega, brisk movement, exercise, a game; also the mechanic's play — the slack that lets a part move
cards.say: Play is the slack that lets a part move. Too tight and it seizes; too loose and it rattles; the game is in between.

cards.from: Old English hwī, hwȳ — the INSTRUMENTAL CASE of hwæt, what: by what, by what means; kin: what, who, how, whether
cards.say: Why is what in the instrumental case: by what means. The title of this deck already had its last card in it.
